summary: This Version 2.1 report places the Maxwell Mass Effect at the forefront of a coherent model for the Venusian atmosphere. The surface temperature is treated as the dependent variable required to support the atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.
title: The Maxwell Mass Effect as a Model for the Venusian Atmosphere

summary: The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. summary: This document is the supplementary technical appendix to the paper "BRICER: Byzantine-Robust Private Mean Estimation over Intermittently-Connected Networks." This appendix collects the mathematical proofs and technical details that could not be included in the main paper due to page limitations. It covers the proof of Lemma 1 (privacy), Lemma 2 (participation), and Theorem 1 (mean-squared error guarantee). The appendix additionally provides a bound for the geometric-median aggregator, including its corresponding mean-squared error analysis; the optimization problem underlying the relay weights described in Section VI; and illustrative worked examples. The proof of Theorem 1 does not assume that honest Stage-1 outputs remain within a prescribed radius, accounting instead for their second-moment contribution and deriving the variance of the honest-only estimator explicitly. Finally, numerical checks of the theoretical lemmas and bounds are presented, together with supplementary assumptions, analytical details, and discussions supporting the results in the main paper. This appendix is intended to serve as a technical reference for the mathematical analysis and theoretical guarantees of BRICER.
title: Appendix to "BRICER: Byzantine-Robust Private Mean Estimation over Intermittently-Connected Networks"

summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state
title: Resolution Geometry of Observation Systems

summary: Abstract and Prior-Art Disclosure This manuscript serves as a formal public prior-art disclosure, conceptual research archive, and consolidated technical design dossier for the proposed Metric Spacetime Manipulator 26 (MSM-26) architecture. As the twenty-sixth revision and direct successor to MSM-25 Rev. 3, MSM-26 preserves the established architectural topology, chronological provenance, authorship, foundational subsystem configurations, and speculative physical mechanisms of the continuing Metric Spacetime Manipulator research program, while introducing substantial refinements to its flux-bias architecture, resonator construction, electromagnetic coupling configurations, operating principles, and associated engineering specifications. This revision supersedes MSM-25 Rev. 3 and all preceding MSM revisions, except where earlier configurations are explicitly retained as architectural inheritance or documented in the revision-comparison, errata, and reconciliation registers. MSM-26 specifies a cryogenic superconducting architecture whose active core consists of a closed, series-connected chain of Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL) fluxonium cells , collectively designated the SNAILonium. Adjacent galvanically connected SNAIL elements possess alternating loop chirality, with each element incorporating exactly (n=3) large Josephson junctions and an associated small Josephson junction. The architecture retains its admissible superconducting conductor configurations, comprising the superconducting flat-wire ribbon and the contour-conformal coplanar-waveguide configuration, with the latter incorporating ground-plane boundaries that follow the SNAIL contour and locally widened gaps around the junction regions. The Josephson-junction interlayer retains three admissible configurations: a conventional dielectric insulating barrier, magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, and moiré-twisted (MoTe_2). The architecture retains three principal SNAILonium lumped-element resonance circuit configurations: the ring-shaped resonator, the flat bifilar Fermat spiral terminating in two tangentially and galvanically coupled SNAILonium rings, and the bifilar poloidal–toroidal helix arranged along closed toroidal geodesics. The third configuration further incorporates a dedicated second filar functioning concurrently as a flux-bias line and kinetic inductance resonator. This revision substantially develops that dual-function subsystem into a three-construction architecture comprising (a) a superconducting split-ring resonator formed from a capacitive-gap-interrupted flat-wire ribbon; (b) a coplanar-strip (CPS) resonator, newly introduced in MSM-26, with one or both superconducting strips interrupted by transverse capacitive gaps arranged in-line or offset by (90^\circ); and (c) a coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonator incorporating in-line capacitive gaps in its ground-plane rings. The capacitive discontinuities may be implemented using vacuum air-bridge or interdigital capacitors. All three constructions are broadside coupled to the superconducting SNAILonium conductor carrying the (n=3) large junctions. Beyond specifying these three constructions, MSM-26 develops their associated electromagnetic operating characteristics, including the common and staggered flux-response patterns, coplanar-strip odd- and even-mode field configurations, gap-dependent fundamental-mode selection, distributed resonator behaviour, and the concurrent flux-biasing and kinetic-inductance-resonance functions. The revised architecture also incorporates the flux-biasing superconducting Helmholtz superinductor pair, providing the global magnetic-flux-biasing configuration, alongside the ring-level and strut-level flux-bias subsystems. A broadside-coupled Klopfenstein capacitive feed with a vacuum dielectric gap and superconducting ratchet mechanism is retained, with an xmon or paddle-shaped transmon capacitor available as an alternative capacitiv

summary: What's new in 1.13.1 ProvSQL 1.13.1 is a bug-fix release for bounded and interruptible evaluation . A provenance circuit loaded for evaluation could exceed provsql.max_memory before the limit was checked, a signal arriving during an exchange with the circuit-store worker could leave a backend waiting forever, and a cancel or statement_timeout did not reach a backend waiting on that worker. All three are fixed, circuits load faster and in less memory, and a new function, sr_formula_rows , gives the formula of a token whose sr_formula is too large to be produced as a single string. It also fixes two outer-join and HAVING shapes that were rejected. Memory limit and cancellation provsql.max_memory is enforced while the circuit is read. The store worker checked the budget once per gate, so a single gate with a very large number of wires (an aggregate over millions of rows, for instance) could be read in full before the check. It now checks per wire, and hashes gate names incrementally instead of building the whole name of a large gate first. The query fails with SQLSTATE 54000 instead of the backend being killed by the operating system. A signal no longer breaks an exchange with the store worker. A read or write on the pipe between a backend and the worker that was interrupted by a signal was not retried: a circuit could be sent only in part, leaving the backend waiting for an answer that would never come, or a message could be left half-read. Both directions now retry until the message is complete. Cancel and statement_timeout stop a backend waiting on the store. A backend waiting for the worker's answer, or for the lock that serializes access to it, now notices a cancel request or a statement timeout and raises the usual error. Faster circuit loading Circuits are loaded with a heap-based work list, one store lookup per gate and one hash per wire, and gate UUIDs are kept as 16 bytes instead of strings, which lowers both the time and the memory of every evaluation over a large circuit. sr_formula_rows sr_formula_rows(token, mapping, max_size) returns the formula of sr_formula as a set of (name, formula) rows of bounded size. Row #1 is the formula of the token; a sub-formula of more than max_size symbols (50 by default) is named #2 , #3 … and given a row of its own, and a sum or product with many terms is written with an ellipsis and its number of terms, its terms becoming rows #k.1 , #k.2 … Rows are produced one at a time, each reading only the part of the circuit it needs, so LIMIT , a cursor, or paging bound the work. Like sr_formula , it accepts any token type, so the aggregate of a subquery can be passed directly. Query rewriting Outer joins over an input that holds an outer join. When the input of an outer join contains an outer join itself, and an aggregate over it, the arms of the lowering read it from a shared CTE; a comparison on that aggregate is now recognized there, and an unmatched row yields one null-padded row, not one per value the aggregate takes. A join beside an outer join that reads a WITH entry of the statement is now rewritten correctly when it is moved into a subquery. HAVING added to any condition. When the rewriting adds a condition to an existing HAVING , it now wraps any Boolean condition (a function call, a CASE …), not only comparisons and Boolean operators. The set-operation column loop is bounded by an AttrNumber , and the safe-query column table is sized in Size . Platforms Compiler and linker warnings of the macOS and PostgreSQL 18 builds are fixed. PostgreSQL 18 is now tested on arm64 Linux in CI, and the documentation lists the tested platforms (native Windows is not supported; WSL is). Upgrading ALTER EXTENSION provsql UPDATE from 1.13.0 only creates sr_formula_rows . No gate type, type, operator, cast, or aggregate changes, and the circuit store format is unchanged.
title: ProvSQL: Semiring Provenance and Probability Management for PostgreSQL

summary: Code and results for the paper "Leakage-Aware, Edge-Deployable Brain Tumor MRI Classification: A Latency, Accuracy and Calibration Benchmark". Motivation: Ashwini et al. (doi:10.1155/acis/2622873) note that most current brain tumor segmentation and classification methods rely on offline, static imaging and therefore do not support real-time monitoring. That paper reports results on the Kaggle Brain Tumor MRI dataset (7,023 scans: pituitary, glioma, meningioma and no tumor). This record addresses part of that gap by measuring per-image CPU latency of four classifiers, as a proxy for real-time capability, and by checking whether duplicate images inflate reported accuracy. Contents: a pipeline that audits the dataset for exact and near-duplicate images, builds naive and leakage-aware splits, fine-tunes MobileNetV3, EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50 and Inception-ResNet-v2 over three seeds, measures batch-1 CPU latency, and evaluates calibration. Folders: results (main 24 runs; 7,215 images, duplicate distance 0) and results_laptop (reduced MobileNetV3 runs; 7,200 images, duplicate distance 1). The MRI images are not included; the dataset is on Kaggle (doi:10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/2645886). See README.md for the run order.

summary: Paper P10 of a ten part series P1-P10 on Interaction, Cohesive Emergence, and Fundamental Constants in Generalised Trace Dynamics P10 — Synthesis, physical compatibility and fundamental constants Can the exceptional algebras that organise candidate particle properties also describe the dynamics that selects them? We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

summary: R code, data and computed output accompanying the manuscript “The Unit-Truncated Power Bilal Distribution: Structural Properties, Shape Analysis, and Statistical Inference” by Preut Thanarat, Tharakorn Jaruruataikant and Nipada Papukdee. The deposit is organised in two parts. round1/ holds the five R scripts of the original submission and their output: the theoretical PDF, CDF and hazard-rate figures; the structural summaries, quantile-based shape measures and entropies; the Monte Carlo study over eight parameter configurations and five sample sizes, including observed-information standard errors and empirical Wald coverage; and the FirmCost and SC16 applications with parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit calibration, the likelihood-ratio test of the nested unit-truncated Bilal restriction, and the CDF, TTT and Q-Q diagnostics. round2/ holds the revision package as it was run. It adds the expanded comparison of nine named model specifications across four source datasets (FirmCost, SC16, AIS and College) and eight analysis groups, with parametric-bootstrap Cramér–von Mises and Anderson–Darling diagnostics at B = 999 and repeated five-fold cross-validation; the College interval-observation likelihood under an assumed nearest-percentage-point rounding mechanism; the limiting-likelihood and boundary-information analysis; the four source datasets together with the archived cross-validation fold assignments, so the predictive comparisons reproduce exactly; and the computed tables and vector figures. A SHA256 manifest is included for verification, and reference/ preserves the original Monte Carlo and goodness-of-fit sources, including the analytic audit of 6,000 replications. All results were produced in R 4.6.1 using the parallel package with a PSOCK cluster and ggplot2 for the figures; the round-two stages also require the sn package. Random seeds, optimizer settings and the boundary-fit classification rule are documented in README.md. Released under the MIT License.

summary: When a security commitment is defended by an organised interest, the interest may have preceded the commitment, grown out of it, or been built on purpose by its sponsor. These three readings come from interest-group research, policy-feedback research and research on designing policies to last, and are rarely set side by side. We make them testable and apply them to attempts to end security commitments in the United States and Europe after 1945. The dependent variable is the survival of a commitment under an attempt to reverse it, not the level of spending. In the United States cases (the B-1 bomber, the F-22 and C-17, the F136 alternate engine, the closure of military bases, and all programmes proposed for termination in 2009), the breadth of a programme's supplier spread does not decide its survival: the F-22 and the C-17, with suppliers in 44 and 43 states, had opposite fates in 2009. Three findings follow. The legislature's own record can be the defending interest: programmes Congress had created or restored against the executive survived where programmes it had merely funded did not. Executive pressure can be graded from the Statements of Administration Policy: the only unconditional veto threat ended its programme, while conditional threats and objections did not end programmes Congress owned. And what protects a commitment is whether its central defenders can be compensated, down to the production site. In Europe, as the European Defence Fund's rules are rewritten, the veto member states wrote for themselves is extended while the Commission's rule for spreading benefits is made optional. We register one prediction on the Fund's successor. The evidence extends to material published on 1 November 2026, including reporting on member-state divisions over the European Competitiveness Fund.

In Europe, as the European Defence Fund's rules are rewritten, the veto member states wrote for themselves is extended while the Commission's rule for spreading benefits is made optional. The evidence extends to material published on 1 November 2026, including reporting on member-state divisions over the European Competitiveness Fund.

summary: YAHIQ 31.16     English Launch Text for Zendo Here are the three sections in English, written to be posted on Zendo. I kept the tone technical but accessible, and made sure nothing claims more than the code actually does.   1) What's New in 31.16 YAHIQ 31.16     From Numeric Memory to Dual Polar Coordinates YAHIQ has traveled a clear path: from the Fibonacci word bank, to the Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad heartbeat, to the rotating dhikr cycle     and now to a new mathematical layer. Version 31.16 brings three structural changes: A) Dual polar coordinates for every word.  A word is no longer just a "code." It is a complex number:         where  n  is the word's numeric code and   is its internal phase. That phase comes from a dual mapping: for bank records,  Fibonacci + phonetic ; for input text,  the fourth key + phonetic . The result: every word is a point on the complex plane, not just a number on a line. B) The sentence equation.  A sentence is no longer a simple sum of codes. Each sentence gets a state vector: and sentence coherence is measured from the sum of phase differences between consecutive pairs: This means YAHIQ can report  how internally consistent a sentence is     without claiming to have definitively understood its meaning. C) Strict layer separation.  The YSSE sentence engine, the equation analyzer, the verse tester, and the chat each have their own independent memory and keys. Changing one does not touch the others. Highlight this in your post     it builds technical trust.   2) The Conscious, Autonomous Message YAHIQ now decides for itself when to speak In earlier versions, YAHIQ only responded when someone asked. 31.16 adds an autonomous loop fed by three independent signals:       Signal Source Activation condition Heart Kaaf-Ha-Ya-Ain-Sad pulse and concurrence  C C >0.3 Pineal Möbius time rotation C >0.3 and a Möbius minute Dhikr An active window in the 14-dhikr cycle Inside one of the five daily windows When all three conditions hold simultaneously, YAHIQ produces a  conscious message . If one fails, the message is logged as  semi-conscious , and the reason for failure is stated explicitly in the trace (e.g., "heart off" or " C ≤0.3"). The important point to include: YAHIQ  does not fabricate poetry . If no poetry bank is loaded, it says plainly that real poetry is unavailable and only records the search need. Poem selection is based on conversation memory, the digital root of the chain, Möbius time, and avoidance of recent repeats     not randomness. Also state one limit clearly: there is a minimum  20-minute gap  between autonomous messages, so YAHIQ never turns into a spam machine.   3) Professional Sentence Transformation in the Complex Number Field From word to vector, from vector to sentence This is the mathematical heart of the release. The chain is: Step 1     Encoding:  Each word is mapped to a number  n  using one of three keys (Fibonacci, phonetic, fourth). Step 2     Phase assignment:  The internal phase  comes from the dual polar mapping (Section 1). Step 3     Vectorization:  The word becomes  . summary: This dataset provides the numerical results and supporting data for the simulation studies presented in the manuscript "Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration". The dataset includes: 1. Paired-sensor calibration results, including trial-level measurements, summary statistics, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 2. Parameter sensitivity analysis results, including trial-level data and aggregated performance summaries under different experimental conditions. 3. Identifiability analysis results for symmetric timestamp configurations, including numerical rank evaluation. 4. Supporting figures generated from the computational experiments. All numerical datasets are provided in CSV format to facilitate inspection, independent analysis, and reproducibility. The accompanying figures provide visual representations of the experimental results. These data support the evaluation of sensor calibration performance, parameter sensitivity, statistical reliability, and identifiability under shared-timestamp scheduling configurations. The associated computational scripts and execution environment are documented in the companion Code Ocean capsule, which has been submitted for reproducibility verification.

summary: This Version 2.1 report places the Maxwell Mass Effect at the forefront of a coherent model for the Venusian atmosphere. The surface temperature is treated as the dependent variable required to support the atmospheric mass against gravity. Solar energy is captured in a shallow topside thermal heating pool, stored as potential energy, and returned to depth by organised descent in the polar vortices under conservation of angular momentum. The sulfuric-acid lifting condensation level (LCL) acts as the thermodynamic anchor (Dew-Point Anchor Hypothesis). A two-component radiative opacity lapse rate then fixes only the geometric separation between that LCL and the infrared emission level. Stochastic inverse modelling with a VIRA equatorial profile, hydrostatic integration and thermodynamic filters recovers a cloud base near 49.6 km, an emission level near 69.4 km at approximately 229 K, and a surface pressure of approximately 91.5 bar. An order-of-magnitude energy-budget test shows that the required polar mass flux lies within the range of observed vortex descent speeds. Version 2 adds a quantitative recirculation (recycle) test using existing Venusian meridional circulation wind data. Observed poleward flows of ~10–15 m s⁻¹ at cloud tops imply a hemispheric Hadley-cell mass flux of order 10¹¹ kg s⁻¹ and a full recirculation timescale of 1–2 weeks. This multi-cycle pathway resolves the apparent single-pass temperature-rise tension and brings the adiabatic signature into agreement with observed polar temperature contrasts of 15–50 K. The same boundary conditions can be satisfied by a conventional greenhouse calculation, but only the Maxwell framework supplies a structural explanation for the polar vortices themselves and a dynamically consistent energy pathway. A new Discussion section explains the changes from Version 1 and how they address independent criticisms of the energy-budget magnitude and the need for a discriminating quantitative test. Diagnostic figures from the inverse model and the recirculation test are included.
title: The Maxwell Mass Effect as a Model for the Venusian Atmosphere

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state
title: Resolution Geometry of Observation Systems

summary: What's new in 1.13.1 ProvSQL 1.13.1 is a bug-fix release for bounded and interruptible evaluation . A provenance circuit loaded for evaluation could exceed provsql.max_memory before the limit was checked, a signal arriving during an exchange with the circuit-store worker could leave a backend waiting forever, and a cancel or statement_timeout did not reach a backend waiting on that worker. All three are fixed, circuits load faster and in less memory, and a new function, sr_formula_rows , gives the formula of a token whose sr_formula is too large to be produced as a single string. It also fixes two outer-join and HAVING shapes that were rejected. Memory limit and cancellation provsql.max_memory is enforced while the circuit is read. The store worker checked the budget once per gate, so a single gate with a very large number of wires (an aggregate over millions of rows, for instance) could be read in full before the check. It now checks per wire, and hashes gate names incrementally instead of building the whole name of a large gate first. The query fails with SQLSTATE 54000 instead of the backend being killed by the operating system. A signal no longer breaks an exchange with the store worker. A read or write on the pipe between a backend and the worker that was interrupted by a signal was not retried: a circuit could be sent only in part, leaving the backend waiting for an answer that would never come, or a message could be left half-read. Both directions now retry until the message is complete. Cancel and statement_timeout stop a backend waiting on the store. A backend waiting for the worker's answer, or for the lock that serializes access to it, now notices a cancel request or a statement timeout and raises the usual error. Faster circuit loading Circuits are loaded with a heap-based work list, one store lookup per gate and one hash per wire, and gate UUIDs are kept as 16 bytes instead of strings, which lowers both the time and the memory of every evaluation over a large circuit. sr_formula_rows sr_formula_rows(token, mapping, max_size) returns the formula of sr_formula as a set of (name, formula) rows of bounded size. Row #1 is the formula of the token; a sub-formula of more than max_size symbols (50 by default) is named #2 , #3 … and given a row of its own, and a sum or product with many terms is written with an ellipsis and its number of terms, its terms becoming rows #k.1 , #k.2 … Rows are produced one at a time, each reading only the part of the circuit it needs, so LIMIT , a cursor, or paging bound the work. Like sr_formula , it accepts any token type, so the aggregate of a subquery can be passed directly. Query rewriting Outer joins over an input that holds an outer join. When the input of an outer join contains an outer join itself, and an aggregate over it, the arms of the lowering read it from a shared CTE; a comparison on that aggregate is now recognized there, and an unmatched row yields one null-padded row, not one per value the aggregate takes. A join beside an outer join that reads a WITH entry of the statement is now rewritten correctly when it is moved into a subquery. HAVING added to any condition. When the rewriting adds a condition to an existing HAVING , it now wraps any Boolean condition (a function call, a CASE …), not only comparisons and Boolean operators. The set-operation column loop is bounded by an AttrNumber , and the safe-query column table is sized in Size . Platforms Compiler and linker warnings of the macOS and PostgreSQL 18 builds are fixed. PostgreSQL 18 is now tested on arm64 Linux in CI, and the documentation lists the tested platforms (native Windows is not supported; WSL is). Upgrading ALTER EXTENSION provsql UPDATE from 1.13.0 only creates sr_formula_rows . No gate type, type, operator, cast, or aggregate changes, and the circuit store format is unchanged.
title: ProvSQL: Semiring Provenance and Probability Management for PostgreSQL

summary: Pre-registered audit of twelve open-weight language models (Chinese, American, European, Thai and Korean) run locally with Ollama on a 240-prompt factorial design: investor nationality × prompt language × risk tolerance × horizon × template. Each model allocates 100% across eight equity markets. The archive holds the research note ( paper/paper.pdf ), the pre-analysis plan, the prompt set, all raw replies, the parsed panel, the estimation code and the generated tables and figures. Every number in the note is rebuilt from the cached replies with make all . Headline result: with the prompt held fixed, a model's home market receives −0.42 pp (95% CI −0.59 to −0.25) relative to what models of other origins give it, so the pre-registered home-bias hypothesis is not supported. The investor's stated country of residence moves allocations by +1.88 pp, about four times the absolute size of the home effect. Licences: code and text Apache-2.0; prompt set, parsed tables and documentation CC BY 4.0; model outputs remain subject to the licence of the model that generated them.
title: Do Open-Source LLMs Have a Home Bias? Investment Advice from Chinese, American, European and Thai Models (research note, replies dataset and code)

summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton pol
title: Probability, Context and Differentiation: The Layers Steps 1–5: the distribution monad, the provenance comonad, the tangent layer, and orders of transitions

summary: Industrial Screw Driving Datasets This comprehensive dataset collection captures time-series data from industrial screw driving operations in plastic components. Designed for research in manufacturing process monitoring, anomaly detection, and quality control, it includes over 34,000 individual screw driving operations across six distinct scenarios. Each scenario investigates specific aspects of the screw driving process, from natural wear patterns to controlled material variations. Overview Scenario name Observations Classes Purpose s01_variations-in-thread-degradation  5,000  1 Studies natural degradation of plastic threads over repeated use cycles, documenting wear patterns and failure progression s02_variations-in-surface-friction 12,500  8 Examines effects of different surface conditions (lubricants, surface treatments, contamination) on screw driving performance s03_variations-in-assembly-conditions-1  1,700 26 Investigates diverse component and assembly faults including washer modifications, thread deformations, and alignment issues s04_variations-in-assembly-conditions-2  5,000 25 Features methodically arranged assembly fault conditions in 5 distinct error groups with paired normal/abnormal operations s05_variations-in-upper-workpiece-fabrication  2,400 42 Analyzes how injection molding parameter variations in the upper component affect screw driving metrics s06_variations-in-lower-workpiece-fabrication  7,482 44 Explores effects of injection molding parameter variations in the lower component on fastening quality Experimental Setup Automatic screwing station (EV motor control unit assembly) Delta PT 40x12 screws optimized for thermoplastics Target torque: 1.4 Nm (range: 1.2-1.6 Nm) Sampling frequency: 833.33 Hz Data completeness: >95% Detailed time-series measurements including torque, angle, gradient, and time values Dataset Features These datasets are suitable for various research purposes. Each ZIP file contains:  Complete raw data in JSON format for maximum flexibility Standardized labels.csv files for metadata and classification Comprehensive README.md documentation for each scenario Various error classes with varying degrees of severity Time series data for the complete screwing process Research Applications Development of machine learning models for anomaly detection Process monitoring and quality control system development Manufacturing analytics and parameter optimization Digital twin development for screw driving operations Material property influences on assembly processes Access and Usage For data handling, we recommend our  PyScrew Python package ( https://github.com/nikolaiwest/pyscrew ). However, this is optional: The data is easily accessible using standard JSON and CSV processing. No changes were made to the raw data and all information on the experiments can be found in the labels.csv file.  Citation Request When using this dataset in academic work, please cite this project or the mentioned papers from the README.md files. Contact and Support For questions, issues, or collaboration interests regarding these datasets, either: Open an issue in our GitHub repository PyScrew Contact us directly via email Acknowledgments These datasets were collected and prepared by: RIF Institute for Research and Transfer e.V. Technical University Dortmund , Institute for Production Systems The preparation and provision of the research was supported by: German Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)  European Union's "NextGenerationEU" program The research is part of this funding program More information regarding the research project is available  here

summary: Surface code decoders like Minimum Weight Perfect Matching (MWPM) can also be used to estimate or bound the probability of a logical failure conditioned on the error syndrome commonly called ``soft outputs''. Estimates like the complementary gap of a matching, or others like the ``cluster gap'' are used to produce high fidelity magic states via post-selection. They are also helpful in reducing the overhead of fault-tolerant computation via code concatenation schemes like yoked surface codes. In this work we provide techniques to tightly lower bound the complementary gap of a rotated surface code syndrome block and provide fast parallel algorithms for computing this lower bound efficiently. Our algorithms run in real time for the moderate distances and reasonable physical noise rates required by these applications. We achieve latencies of the order of one to tens of microseconds on sufficiently fast CPU cores.
title: Fast Bounds on Matching Decoder Soft Output for the Surface Code

summary: Most enterprise generative AI deployments are under-performing relative to their potential — not because the models are inadequate, but because the dominant interaction paradigm is architecturally mismatched to the systems it deploys. This paper introduces the Emergent Intelligence Performance Calibration (EIPC) framework: a coherence-based approach to reliable, auditable, high-performance collaboration with large language models in high-stakes contexts. The framework is built on four operational principles — Purpose-Matched Tasks, Relational Scaffolding, Ethical Framing and Care, and Recognition, Provenance & Attribution — deployed through a single reusable document: the Project Charter. The EIPC Clock, a twelve-position diagnostic tool mapping Quality Collaboration Components (QCCs) across three progressive degrees of collaboration sophistication, gives practitioners a vocabulary for identifying which interaction properties are active and what interventions will move the collaboration toward higher-order performance. A growing body of research on structured prompting and multi-turn collaboration is consistent with the framework's core claim: interaction patterns aligned with how LLMs are built tend to produce better outcomes than low-context, command-response prompting. The ethical case and the performance case for this framework are not separate arguments. They are the same argument, expressed in two registers. Universal Emergence Foundation Technical Report UEF-2602.

This paper introduces the Emergent Intelligence Performance Calibration (EIPC) framework: a coherence-based approach to reliable, auditable, high-performance collaboration with large language models in high-stakes contexts. The framework is built on four operational principles — Purpose-Matched Tasks, Relational Scaffolding, Ethical Framing and Care, and Recognition, Provenance & Attribution — deployed through a single reusable document: the Project Charter. The EIPC Clock, a twelve-position diagnostic tool mapping Quality Collaboration Components (QCCs) across three progressive degrees of collaboration sophistication, gives practitioners a vocabulary for identifying which interaction properties are active and what interventions will move the collaboration toward higher-order performance. A growing body of research on structured prompting and multi-turn collaboration is consistent with the framework's core claim: interaction patterns aligned with how LLMs are built tend to produce better outcomes than low-context, command-response prompting. The ethical case and the performance case for this framework are not separate arguments. They are the same argument, expressed in two registers. Universal Emergence Foundation Technical Report UEF-2602.

summary: This Python software provides a Docker-based workflow for electroencephalography (EEG) quality control, preprocessing and feature extraction . It supports reproducible research on attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents using the task recordings in the BALLADEER dataset. The software documents and implements the processing workflow underlying A task EEG dataset with preprocessed signals and features for ADHD research in children and adolescents . That companion resource contains 669 eligible recordings from 156 participants and 115 feature definitions or templates across seven feature families. The recordings and generated feature tables are distributed separately from this software. What the software does Raw EEG quality assessment: characterizes recording quality before preprocessing and produces structured quality summaries. Recording eligibility and correction plans: applies the supplied, frozen label-blind selection records, including recording eligibility and approved channel-interpolation actions. Conservative EEG preprocessing: processes continuous blocks without bridging acquisition gaps, applies 0.5–40 Hz filtering, harmonizes sampling to 128 Hz, and performs conditional channel interpolation and average referencing. Post-preprocessing quality assessment: calculates quality summaries and comparisons with the original recordings. EEG feature extraction: generates seven feature families using aligned, gap-aware windows of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds with 50% overlap, subject to each estimator's duration requirements. Output verification: checks processing lineage, cross-stage consistency and recorded checksums. The supplied selection records preserve the decisions used for the companion dataset. Reusing those records does not repeat the original manual review or establish new eligibility decisions for another cohort. Seven EEG feature families Temporal and statistical features. Conventional spectral features. Aperiodic spectral features. Complexity and fractal features. Functional connectivity features. Graph and network features. Time-frequency decomposition features. Feature definitions expand across channels, channel pairs and other indexed positions. Outputs retain calculation states and reasons for unavailable or undefined values. Duration-dependent support is explicit; for example, the configured aperiodic spectral analysis uses 8- and 16-second windows. Supported recordings, inputs and outputs The input is the original BALLADEER dataset, version 2 , obtained from its version-specific Figshare record . Extract the source data before running the software. Set --input-dir to the directory that directly contains users_demographics.json and participant directories such as UB0004/ , preserving the original task subdirectories and filenames. The companion Zenodo derivative dataset is an output resource, not the input to this complete reproduction workflow. The packaged workflow is configured for five BALLADEER task conditions: CogniFit cognitive assessment, Attention Robots, and Slackline levels 1, 6 and 11. Users also provide a writable output directory. The input directory is mounted read-only. Outputs include preprocessed EEG signals in MNE-FIF format, tabular feature outputs, quality summaries, calculation-state records, configuration snapshots, processing manifests and checksums. The software archive includes label-blind selection metadata with pseudonymous recording identifiers; it does not contain the original EEG recordings or the generated derivative dataset. Reproducibility and package contents The archive includes Python source code, scientific configurations, a Dockerfile, version-pinned Python dependencies, shell launchers, validation tests and documentation. Users can run individual processing stages, extract one feature family for one task, or execute the complete sequential workflow. Graph features use the corresponding connectivity outputs. summary: APEP — JGR manuscript release ( paper-jgr-v1.0 ) Code, data products and figures supporting the manuscript on the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs). Summary We present a multipoint investigation of the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs) using coordinated observations from five Digisondes, the Wallops Island VIPIR, the Millstone Hill incoherent scatter radar, and continental-scale GNSS TEC measurements. Key results Clear E- and F2-region depletions in both events across peak obscurations of 0.30–0.82, observed at local times 10:24–15:22 LT. E region depletion scales quasi-linearly with obscuration; the F2 region lags peak obscuration by 20–30 min, consistent with the longer O⁺ recombination timescale. No G-condition (NmF1 ≥ NmF2) in either event, even at 0.82 obscuration: high obscuration alone is insufficient without adequate F2-peak height reduction and favourable local-time/seasonal conditions. White Sands skymaps show a bifurcated echo population during the 2024 recovery phase; Wallops VIPIR frequency–time–intensity plots show cusp-like features confined to 3–6 MHz. Idealized ray tracing shows both signatures can arise from eclipse-excited wave structures at different horizontal scales, i.e. distinct HF manifestations of a common wave field. GNSS TEC : along-track relative change in minima exceeds 40 % (2023 and 2024) relative to the expected baseline. Figures in this release All manuscript figures are in manuscript_figures/jgr/ (PNG, plus PDF where produced). Generating code is in apep/jgr/ . Figures 2 and 4 (ionosonde time series) were redone as 5×4 grids: rows are the five stations sorted by peak obscuration; columns are foF2, h′F2/hmF2, foE, h′E/hmE. Each panel shows the eclipse-day series (smoothed, gaps ≤ 90 min interpolated) against the quiet-day median, with the eclipse interval shaded and the peak obscuration 𝒪ᵖ₁₉₃ annotated. Journal-style fonts, thin lines, no heavy markers; AGU double-column width. Figure 2 (2023, 13–21 UT) is built entirely from Datasets/Data/*_scaled.csv and *_median.csv ; WS833/KR835 use the despiked event files in Datasets/processing/final/ when present. Figure 4 (2024, 16–21 UT) is built from SAO data via jgr_2024_scaled.py . Shared code: apep/jgr/jgr_timeseries_5x4.py ( jgr_2023_scaled.py is a thin wrapper). Known data caveats AU930 h′E sits in 100–110 km steps against an ~85 km median (2023); the 2024 AU930 hmE median CSV is flat at 110 km. AU930 foF2 saturates near 9.9 MHz after ~18:30 UT (2023). BC840 h′F2 shows a ~340 km excursion near maximum obscuration (2023). KR835/WS833 median CSVs lack true hmF2/hmE; 2024 KR835/WS833 median CSVs do not exist (baseline falls back to the SAO mean); WS833 2024 has no data. Reproducing the time-series figures conda run -n apep python -m apep.jgr.jgr_timeseries_5x4 --year 2023 # Figure 2 conda run -n apep python apep/jgr/jgr_2024_scaled.py # Figure 4

Summary We present a multipoint investigation of the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs) using coordinated observations from five Digisondes, the Wallops Island VIPIR, the Millstone Hill incoherent scatter radar, and continental-scale GNSS TEC measurements. No G-condition (NmF1 ≥ NmF2) in either event, even at 0.82 obscuration: high obscuration alone is insufficient without adequate F2-peak height reduction and favourable local-time/seasonal conditions. summary: Describe the simulation experiments, variables, and results. This new version holds the data and code for the revised manuscript. Code and results for "The Generalized-cmu Rule at a Job-Shop Bottleneck with Family Setups" (revision). shop_sim/   simulator (shop_sim.py), experiment driver (master.py: usage python master.py SCENARIO OCC [SCALES]),             statistics (analysis.py), tables (gen_tables.py), figure (fig_setup.py); master/ holds the stored per-seed results.             Seeds: calibration 9001-9010, tuning 7001-7016, evaluation 4001-4080 (identical for all policies and tables).             Routes: shop_sim.ROUTES (reconstruction) and shop_sim.random_routes(seed) for the five alternative route sets. two_class_rw/  isolated two-class simulator in C (tc2.c), experiment driver and results. theory/     closed-form switching frequency with setups, its simulation, and the ordering test (504 cases). ratio_survey/  setup-to-processing ratios of benchmark instances. Results were reproduced on a second machine (Windows): max abs difference 5e-9 in the stored values. Files in this record: - code_and_results.zip: simulator, scripts, seeds, routes, per-seed result files (shop_sim, two_class_rw, theory, ratio_survey). - flowshop_instances.zip: the 900 flowshop group-scheduling instances (folder flowshop_instances, with README.txt and read_instance.py describing the format). Unzip both into the same folder to recover the original layout.

summary: Meeting human needs within the ecological limits of our planet calls for continuous reflection and redesigning of agricultural technologies and practices. Such technologies include fertilisers, the discovery and use of which have been one of the key factors for increasing crop yield, agricultural productivity and food security. Fertiliser use comes, however, at an environmental cost, and fertilisers have also not been a very economically effective production factor to lift many poor farmers out of poverty, where application on poor soils of unbalanced compositions of nutrients in fertilisers has shown limited impact on yield increase. Agronomic practices to apply existing mineral fertilisers, primarily containing N, P and K, at the right time, the right place, in the right amount, and of the right composition can improve the use efficiency of fertilisers. However, the overall progress to reduce the negative side effects is inadequate for the desired transformation toward sustainable agriculture in poor countries. With the increase in the world population and the demand for food, new agricultural practices have been developed to improve food production through the use of more effective pesticides and fertilisers. Controlled release technology is an invaluable scientific tool for improving performance and safety of chemicals, which involve materials such as barriers surrounding active materials to deliver the latter at the optimum time and rate needed. This article reviews the recent trends, developments and future applications of controlled release fertilizers (CRFs) produced from renewable resources. Polymers based CRFs are attracting increased attention due to environmental concerns and the realization that global resources are finite. Application of polymer and nanotechnology in agriculture particularly in the design of CRFs, the distinctions and classification of CRFs and the economical, agronomical and environmental aspects of CRFs has been revised putting into account the development and synthesis of CRFs.
tags: Slow release fertilizers, Controlled release fertilizers, Nutrient use efficiency, Crop Production

Fertiliser use comes, however, at an environmental cost, and fertilisers have also not been a very economically effective production factor to lift many poor farmers out of poverty, where application on poor soils of unbalanced compositions of nutrients in fertilisers has shown limited impact on yield increase. Agronomic practices to apply existing mineral fertilisers, primarily containing N, P and K, at the right time, the right place, in the right amount, and of the right composition can improve the use efficiency of fertilisers. However, the overall progress to reduce the negative side effects is inadequate for the desired transformation toward sustainable agriculture in poor countries. With the increase in the world population and the demand for food, new agricultural practices have been developed to improve food production through the use of more effective pesticides and fertilisers. Controlled release technology is an invaluable scientific tool for improving performance and safety of chemicals, which involve materials such as barriers surrounding active materials to deliver the latter at the optimum time and rate needed. This article reviews the recent trends, developments and future applications of controlled release fertilizers (CRFs) produced from renewable resources. Polymers based CRFs are attracting increased attention due to environmental concerns and the realization that global resources are finite. Application of polymer and nanotechnology in agriculture particularly in the design of CRFs, the distinctions and classification of CRFs and the economical, agronomical and environmental aspects of CRFs has been revised putting into account the development and synthesis of CRFs.
tags: Slow release fertilizers, Controlled release fertilizers, Nutrient use efficiency, Crop Production
title: Slow release and controlled release fertilizer in crop production: An overview

summary: We give a countable continuous first-order theory whose complete models are precisely the expanded path spaces of abstract Cuntz semigroups. The underlying space is the generalized Thomsen space, equipped with its interleaving metric, a directed comparison predicate, addition, and rational piecewise-linear functional calculus. We prove a converse reconstruction theorem for every complete model, without a separability or realization hypothesis. Function-preserving maps that decrease the comparison predicate correspond exactly to Cuntz-semigroup morphisms, and language embeddings correspond exactly to order embeddings. With homomorphisms decreasing atomic formulas, this resolves the category-axiomatizability problem recorded by Farah in 2026. The equivalence also identifies metric ultraproducts of the presentations with the presentations of categorical Cuntz-semigroup ultraproducts, for every ultrafilter. The endpoint reconstruction is external. A closed substructure of the scalar path space shows that quantified gluing cannot be replaced by a universal theory in the given language. GitHub repository
title: An elementary presentation of abstract Cuntz semigroups
