summary: This dataset provides the numerical results and supporting data for the simulation studies presented in the manuscript "Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration". The dataset includes: 1. Paired-sensor calibration results, including trial-level measurements, summary statistics, and bootstrap confidence intervals. 2. Parameter sensitivity analysis results, including trial-level data and aggregated performance summaries under different experimental conditions. 3. Identifiability analysis results for symmetric timestamp configurations, including numerical rank evaluation. 4. Supporting figures generated from the computational experiments. All numerical datasets are provided in CSV format to facilitate inspection, independent analysis, and reproducibility. The accompanying figures provide visual representations of the experimental results. These data support the evaluation of sensor calibration performance, parameter sensitivity, statistical reliability, and identifiability under shared-timestamp scheduling configurations. The associated computational scripts and execution environment are documented in the companion Code Ocean capsule, which has been submitted for reproducibility verification.
title: Identifiability and Scheduling for Shared-Timestamp Polynomial Sensor Calibration

summary: Reference release of ProvChain, a permissioned blockchain research prototype in which participating organizations share ontology packages as semantic contracts for traceability events and provenance validation. This release contains the Rust reference system (durable journal behind one fail-closed Final Admission boundary, governance-authenticated membership with three-node Proof-of-Authority convergence, package-declared staged-union SHACL enforcement with SPACL-backed subclass reasoning, participant-controlled privacy lifecycle, and a bounded receipt-backed bridge), ontology packages and SHACL validation assets, GS1/EPCIS-oriented example payloads, public benchmark artifacts, and the end-to-end reference-system correctness-campaign evidence archive (recorded runs, conformance vectors, raw logs, hashes, and mechanically derived manifests) under test_reports/reference-evidence/ .
title: ProvChain: A Shared-Ontology Semantic Blockchain Framework for Traceability (reference release)

summary: This repository contains the data construction and analysis code accompanying a study of recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries. The source history covers July 2013–December 2019. The primary estimation panel covers July 2014–December 2019, allowing a complete preceding-12-month predictor window, and contains 1,650 country-month observations and 58 reactive request-months. The package includes retained source and coding inputs, derived analysis datasets, Python scripts, manuscript tables and figures, and documentation of variable construction and software requirements. Analyses include the primary between–within logistic model, alternative windows and outcomes, country exclusions, leave-one-country-out models, a direct between–within coefficient contrast, separate baseline-covariate adjustments, and calendar-year and outcome-month-inclusive sensitivities. The repository also includes a human-coded external-documentation audit of 22 reactive request-months with zero recorded activity in the preceding 12 months. The audit distinguishes documentation within the same country and window from identification of the outbreak targeted by a particular request. The activity predictor measures recorded active outbreak-months, not case counts or outbreak-to-request delay. Source provenance, coding decisions, and unresolved questions are documented in the package. See README.md for execution instructions.
title: Data and analysis code for recorded cholera outbreak activity and reactive oral cholera vaccine requests in 25 African countries, 2013–2019

summary: The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton polyhedron,
title: Probability, Context and Differentiation: The Layers Steps 1–4c: the distribution monad, the provenance comonad, the tangent layer, and orders of transitions

summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) agents embedded in software-as-a-service (SaaS) platforms inherit the user's permissions. When a permission is revoked during a task, the platform rejects the next read, but the agent still retains the data it previously retrieved in its context, drafts, saved documents, and memory. This study examined how platforms can enforce a mid-task revocation on that working state. The author defined correct behavior for four revocation types, each mapped to an obligation to block, purge, or suspend, including leaks through paraphrases, aggregates, and existence hints. The author built RevBench, a simulated field-service platform, and compared nine enforcement designs from access control, information-flow control, and machine unlearning on six frontier models in 6,048 runs. Outputs were scored using exact matching and two large-language-model judges. Per-call authorization still failed in 417 of 720 runs (57.9%), rising from 34.4% when the revocation preceded retrieval to 72.8% when it followed delivery. Information-flow labels leaked the least (12.9%) but left revoked data saved in 44.2% of runs. Designs that invalidated the context performed best, while editing the context in place left derived facts behind. A full restart and selective replay with listing-level provenance reached 21.4% and 21.0% substantive failure, the latter with 12.1% fewer model calls. Most remaining failures were disclosures about the restriction, often repeating the platform’s own notice, and larger models did not reduce them. SaaS platforms need revocation controls that reach the agent’s working state and match the type of revocation. Data and code supporting the article "Revoking Access Does Not Revoke Knowledge: Enforcing Mid-Task Permission Changes in AI agents:

title: RevBench: code, scenarios, run logs and judgments for enforcing mid-task permission revocation in AI agents

summary: Resolution Geometry: A Kernel–Stabilizer Geometry of Observability Abstract Resolution Geometry (RG) is a protocol-explicit framework for characterizing what a declared observation system can distinguish, preserve, and consistently infer. Its starting point is a family of observation laws together with admissible outcome relabelings, rather than a covariance decomposition, metric, or dynamical model. Equality of the joint observation law defines a kernel groupoid and an observational quotient, canonically identified with the law image. An experiment-internal quantity is identifiable precisely when it is constant on observational fibres. The quotient alone determines neither a metric nor a connection, causal structure, clock, physical scale, or law of motion. The framework separates exact observational equivalence from statistical distinguishability, admissibility, symmetry, and physical realization. The stabilizer of the observation law induces a faithful effective action on the quotient. Liftable symmetry is distinguished from symmetry of the law image: the former can depend on the latent presentation, whereas the observable layer is presentation-invariant once its law-space structures and declarations are fixed. On regular strata, natural modules defined by pullback from law space descend uniquely to the observational quotient. This gives representative independence and projectability for law-defined structures, without asserting that naturality selects those structures. In regular classical experiments, the Fisher tensor supplies infinitesimal distinguishability under the stated Markov-monotonicity assumptions; its radical agrees with the observational vertical space under the corresponding regularity conditions. Quantum protocols require a declared operational task to select within the family of monotone metrics. A central organizing result concerns task-preserving conversion . For a representation map and a declared family of downstream tasks, RG characterizes the exact set of compatible task outcomes on each representation fibre. Unique inference is possible exactly when this residual is a singleton. Otherwise the appropriate output is a correspondence or a typed abstention, not an arbitrary hidden representative. Pairing a representation with its tasks gives a terminal sufficient refinement. For declared operations, observational closure is expressed by the greatest operation-stable congruence contained in the observation kernel. These constructions distinguish local differential rank, global orbit separation, observational completeness, and reconstruction, and make preservation requirements explicit under composition. Second-order realizations provide concrete classification and computational tools. Under a declared block-orthogonal gauge, a covariance datum is encoded by a symmetric matrix tuple whose ordered word traces form a complete pointwise invariant, including repeated eigenvalues, vanishing couplings, and rank-deficient sectors. On simple-spectrum strata, mixed moments recover coupling magnitudes, while independent cycle holonomies complete the residual sign classification. This distinguishes hidden values omitted by a descriptor from distinctions that are genuinely observationally null . Under the different contract of covariance-preserving block-linear transformations, canonical correlations with multiplicity classify pointwise data; constant-type families additionally carry bundle and gluing information. Pointwise classification therefore does not replace the transport, relative alignment, or global data required by field-level tasks. Across rank, symmetry, and protocol changes, RG uses specialization maps when kernel inclusion permits them and correspondences otherwise. Smooth geometry is confined to its regular domain; proper-groupoid and tame settings support stratified descriptions with slices, tangent cones, and orbit-type changes. Finite-resolution statements are separated from exact model state
title: Resolution Geometry of Observation Systems

summary: Abstract and Prior-Art Disclosure This manuscript serves as a formal public prior-art disclosure, conceptual research archive, and consolidated technical design dossier for the proposed Metric Spacetime Manipulator 26 (MSM-26) architecture. As the twenty-sixth revision and direct successor to MSM-25 Rev. 3, MSM-26 preserves the established architectural topology, chronological provenance, authorship, foundational subsystem configurations, and speculative physical mechanisms of the continuing Metric Spacetime Manipulator research program, while introducing substantial refinements to its flux-bias architecture, resonator construction, electromagnetic coupling configurations, operating principles, and associated engineering specifications. This revision supersedes MSM-25 Rev. 3 and all preceding MSM revisions, except where earlier configurations are explicitly retained as architectural inheritance or documented in the revision-comparison, errata, and reconciliation registers. MSM-26 specifies a cryogenic superconducting architecture whose active core consists of a closed, series-connected chain of Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL) fluxonium cells , collectively designated the SNAILonium. Adjacent galvanically connected SNAIL elements possess alternating loop chirality, with each element incorporating exactly (n=3) large Josephson junctions and an associated small Josephson junction. The architecture retains its admissible superconducting conductor configurations, comprising the superconducting flat-wire ribbon and the contour-conformal coplanar-waveguide configuration, with the latter incorporating ground-plane boundaries that follow the SNAIL contour and locally widened gaps around the junction regions. The Josephson-junction interlayer retains three admissible configurations: a conventional dielectric insulating barrier, magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, and moiré-twisted (MoTe_2). The architecture retains three principal SNAILonium lumped-element resonance circuit configurations: the ring-shaped resonator, the flat bifilar Fermat spiral terminating in two tangentially and galvanically coupled SNAILonium rings, and the bifilar poloidal–toroidal helix arranged along closed toroidal geodesics. The third configuration further incorporates a dedicated second filar functioning concurrently as a flux-bias line and kinetic inductance resonator. This revision substantially develops that dual-function subsystem into a three-construction architecture comprising (a) a superconducting split-ring resonator formed from a capacitive-gap-interrupted flat-wire ribbon; (b) a coplanar-strip (CPS) resonator, newly introduced in MSM-26, with one or both superconducting strips interrupted by transverse capacitive gaps arranged in-line or offset by (90^\circ); and (c) a coplanar-waveguide (CPW) resonator incorporating in-line capacitive gaps in its ground-plane rings. The capacitive discontinuities may be implemented using vacuum air-bridge or interdigital capacitors. All three constructions are broadside coupled to the superconducting SNAILonium conductor carrying the (n=3) large junctions. Beyond specifying these three constructions, MSM-26 develops their associated electromagnetic operating characteristics, including the common and staggered flux-response patterns, coplanar-strip odd- and even-mode field configurations, gap-dependent fundamental-mode selection, distributed resonator behaviour, and the concurrent flux-biasing and kinetic-inductance-resonance functions. The revised architecture also incorporates the flux-biasing superconducting Helmholtz superinductor pair, providing the global magnetic-flux-biasing configuration, alongside the ring-level and strut-level flux-bias subsystems. A broadside-coupled Klopfenstein capacitive feed with a vacuum dielectric gap and superconducting ratchet mechanism is retained, with an xmon or paddle-shaped transmon capacitor available as an alternative capacitiv
title: Metric Spacetime Manipulator 26 (MSM-26)

summary: What's new in 1.13.1 ProvSQL 1.13.1 is a bug-fix release for bounded and interruptible evaluation . A provenance circuit loaded for evaluation could exceed provsql.max_memory before the limit was checked, a signal arriving during an exchange with the circuit-store worker could leave a backend waiting forever, and a cancel or statement_timeout did not reach a backend waiting on that worker. All three are fixed, circuits load faster and in less memory, and a new function, sr_formula_rows , gives the formula of a token whose sr_formula is too large to be produced as a single string. It also fixes two outer-join and HAVING shapes that were rejected. Memory limit and cancellation provsql.max_memory is enforced while the circuit is read. The store worker checked the budget once per gate, so a single gate with a very large number of wires (an aggregate over millions of rows, for instance) could be read in full before the check. It now checks per wire, and hashes gate names incrementally instead of building the whole name of a large gate first. The query fails with SQLSTATE 54000 instead of the backend being killed by the operating system. A signal no longer breaks an exchange with the store worker. A read or write on the pipe between a backend and the worker that was interrupted by a signal was not retried: a circuit could be sent only in part, leaving the backend waiting for an answer that would never come, or a message could be left half-read. Both directions now retry until the message is complete. Cancel and statement_timeout stop a backend waiting on the store. A backend waiting for the worker's answer, or for the lock that serializes access to it, now notices a cancel request or a statement timeout and raises the usual error. Faster circuit loading Circuits are loaded with a heap-based work list, one store lookup per gate and one hash per wire, and gate UUIDs are kept as 16 bytes instead of strings, which lowers both the time and the memory of every evaluation over a large circuit. sr_formula_rows sr_formula_rows(token, mapping, max_size) returns the formula of sr_formula as a set of (name, formula) rows of bounded size. Row #1 is the formula of the token; a sub-formula of more than max_size symbols (50 by default) is named #2 , #3 … and given a row of its own, and a sum or product with many terms is written with an ellipsis and its number of terms, its terms becoming rows #k.1 , #k.2 … Rows are produced one at a time, each reading only the part of the circuit it needs, so LIMIT , a cursor, or paging bound the work. Like sr_formula , it accepts any token type, so the aggregate of a subquery can be passed directly. Query rewriting Outer joins over an input that holds an outer join. When the input of an outer join contains an outer join itself, and an aggregate over it, the arms of the lowering read it from a shared CTE; a comparison on that aggregate is now recognized there, and an unmatched row yields one null-padded row, not one per value the aggregate takes. A join beside an outer join that reads a WITH entry of the statement is now rewritten correctly when it is moved into a subquery. HAVING added to any condition. When the rewriting adds a condition to an existing HAVING , it now wraps any Boolean condition (a function call, a CASE …), not only comparisons and Boolean operators. summary: Paper P10 of a ten part series P1-P10 on Interaction, Cohesive Emergence, and Fundamental Constants in Generalised Trace Dynamics P10 — Synthesis, physical compatibility and fundamental constants Can the exceptional algebras that organise candidate particle properties also describe the dynamics that selects them? We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

summary: When a security commitment is defended by an organised interest, the interest may have preceded the commitment, grown out of it, or been built on purpose by its sponsor. These three readings come from interest-group research, policy-feedback research and research on designing policies to last, and are rarely set side by side. We make them testable and apply them to attempts to end security commitments in the United States and Europe after 1945. The dependent variable is the survival of a commitment under an attempt to reverse it, not the level of spending. In the United States cases (the B-1 bomber, the F-22 and C-17, the F136 alternate engine, the closure of military bases, and all programmes proposed for termination in 2009), the breadth of a programme's supplier spread does not decide its survival: the F-22 and the C-17, with suppliers in 44 and 43 states, had opposite fates in 2009. Three findings follow. The legislature's own record can be the defending interest: programmes Congress had created or restored against the executive survived where programmes it had merely funded did not. Executive pressure can be graded from the Statements of Administration Policy: the only unconditional veto threat ended its programme, while conditional threats and objections did not end programmes Congress owned. And what protects a commitment is whether its central defenders can be compensated, down to the production site. In Europe, as the European Defence Fund's rules are rewritten, the veto member states wrote for themselves is extended while the Commission's rule for spreading benefits is made optional. We register one prediction on the Fund's successor. The evidence extends to material published on 1 November 2026, including reporting on member-state divisions over the European Competitiveness Fund.
title: Grown or Built? Interests that Defend Commitments after 1945

summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton pol
title: Probability, Context and Differentiation: The Layers Steps 1–5: the distribution monad, the provenance comonad, the tangent layer, and orders of transitions

summary: Most enterprise generative AI deployments are under-performing relative to their potential — not because the models are inadequate, but because the dominant interaction paradigm is architecturally mismatched to the systems it deploys. This paper introduces the Emergent Intelligence Performance Calibration (EIPC) framework: a coherence-based approach to reliable, auditable, high-performance collaboration with large language models in high-stakes contexts. The framework is built on four operational principles — Purpose-Matched Tasks, Relational Scaffolding, Ethical Framing and Care, and Recognition, Provenance & Attribution — deployed through a single reusable document: the Project Charter. The EIPC Clock, a twelve-position diagnostic tool mapping Quality Collaboration Components (QCCs) across three progressive degrees of collaboration sophistication, gives practitioners a vocabulary for identifying which interaction properties are active and what interventions will move the collaboration toward higher-order performance. A growing body of research on structured prompting and multi-turn collaboration is consistent with the framework's core claim: interaction patterns aligned with how LLMs are built tend to produce better outcomes than low-context, command-response prompting. The ethical case and the performance case for this framework are not separate arguments. They are the same argument, expressed in two registers. Universal Emergence Foundation Technical Report UEF-2602.
title: Coherence-Based Collaboration & Emergent Intelligence Performance Calibration (EIPC): A Framework and Vocabulary for High-Stakes Work with LLMs

summary: The calibration and test probabilities of every run of a tabular classification benchmark, released so that prediction sets and their metrics can be recomputed without refitting a model. A conformal set is a function of four arrays: the class probabilities and labels on a calibration split, and the same on a test split. This deposit is those arrays, together with the software that reads them. The benchmark comprises 218 classification datasets and 22 models from four families, among them 13 tabular foundation models, each evaluated with the same ten seeds. Of the 218, 178 are real datasets and 40 are a synthetic block generated for this benchmark; three of the real ones are Bayesian-network resamplings of small classical datasets and are much larger than their seeds; of those, only one has its own seed in the collection, so that pair is not independent of itself while a rank test treats datasets as independent. Dataset size does not indicate provenance: the largest datasets in the collection are real. Coverage is not uniform and the per-model dataset count is reported for every cell. Eleven datasets carry more than ten classes, and the in-context models measured on them cannot enter them: one refuses and names the limit, another builds a ten-output head and fails inside a kernel. That is a capability limit observed on the models that were run rather than a property claimed of the family, and it is not missing work. One foundation model is measured on the original datasets only. Anything computed across models should be computed on a complete submatrix: the datasets on which every model being compared has all ten seeds. The calibration rows are held out of fitting, of tuning, of early stopping and of the in-context data, and each cell records which rows they were. The code that does it is included, with the line of each step documented. Probabilities are float64 and are not rounded: a prediction set is a comparison against a threshold, and a point sitting on that threshold moves if the value it is compared to is shortened. The data are released under CC BY 4.0. The software included in the source archive is released under the MIT licence, as stated by the LICENSE file it contains. The datasets themselves are not redistributed: each cell carries the row indices into its source dataset, and the synthetic datasets regenerate from their seeds with an included script. Model weights are not redistributed; every checkpoint is named in the model table. Version 1.2.0 adds the runs completed after version 1.1.0 and changes or removes nothing in it. Three new shards (cells-011 to cells-013, 2.02 GB) hold 311 further cells; index.parquet now lists all 46,182 cells and manifest_1016.parquet is their manifest. The files prefixed blocks_1016__ recompute the two blocks outside the main comparison on the completed runs, with the pipeline that produced the article's tables: the large-dataset block on 49 datasets and 21 models (42 in version 1.1.0) and the many-class block on 11 datasets and 7 models (5 in version 1.1.0). The main block of 113 real datasets and 22 models is unchanged. CHANGELOG.md lists what is added and the pairs that are still missing, with the reason for each.
title: TabSets: calibration and test probabilities for set-valued evaluation of tabular classifiers

summary: 50/60 MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 50/60). It investigates safe failure recovery with preserved productive service. The research coupling is autonomous manufacturing mission x regenerative specimen integrity x physically verified fault recovery. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: A frozen safety and recovery protocol will improve completed qualified work at equal fault burden while meeting independent stop and specimen integrity gates. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-inject four fault classes into complete cell assembly missions with matched useful work targets. Strong comparators include expert human operation, fixed automation scripts and conventional redundant hardware. A central rival account is apparent safety caused by aborting early and completing less useful work. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: no advantage at equal effective work or an unknown fault fails to stop the apparatus. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020. Full external bibliographic DOI checking and scientific peer review have not been completed. Domain-specific sensitivity, causal identifiability and independent replication require qualified laboratory evaluation before any scientific superiority claim. TLOFNC80D30G348Z ) Stato Giuridico-Computazionale: Pienamente operativo ed esecutivo Identificatore di Radice Internazionale (OID): urn:oid:2.5.4.97:IT-TLOFNC80D30G348Z::MSDT-PARCS-ROOT Autorità Internazionale IANA PEN: Private Enterprise Number 66881 (Radice OID Master: 1.3.6.1.4.1.66881 ) Qualificazioni Strategiche di Procurement Internazionale: Codice NATO NCAGE: AY470 (Ministero della Difesa - Direzione Nazionale degli Armamenti) Codice EU PIC (Participant Identification Code): 860441411 (Portale UE Funding & Tenders ) 1. MANIFESTO MSDT: FRAMEWORK NORMATIVO E CIBERNETICO Il presente documento costituisce l'aggiornamento strutturale e l'asseverazione forense definitiva del Framework Europeo MSDT (Metodo Scientifico Digitale Tola) . L'attuale release formalizza l'architettura cibernetica di terzo ordine per il controllo deterministico e la supervisione antropocentrica sui sistemi di Intelligenza Artificiale ad Alto Rischio (piena conformità al Regolamento UE 2024/1689 "AI Act", Art. 14 e Art. 50) . Il framework opera come un ecosistema ad alta densità di token per la gestione della proprietà intellettuale, la validazione crittografica delle competenze educative e scientifiche, e l'interoperabilità plurisettoriale e sistemico-integrata . La radice OID 1.3.6.1.4.1.66881 funge da nodo gerarchico primario da cui dipendono i moduli di interblocco macchina e supervisione umana . 2. CONFORMITÀ FAIR E ARCHITETTURA RO-Crate (RESEARCH OBJECT CRATE) L'intero Archival Information Package (AIP) della Versione 27 è strutturato, indicizzato e rilasciato in piena conformità ai principi FAIR ( Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, Reusable ) tramite l'implementazione nativa dello standard internazionale RO-Crate 1.1 ( ro-crate-metadata.json ) . Questo garantisce che l'opera sia un oggetto di ricerca autosufficiente e macchina-leggibile: Findable (Rintracciabile): Ancoraggio permanente tramite Digital Object Identifier (DOI) globali (Concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20177271 e identificativi di versione) e metadati persistenti registrati nell'albero IANA PEN 66881 . Accessible (Accessibile): Disponibilità dei file in formati standard aperti e protetti, corredati da marcatura PAdES-LTA (orizzonte fiduciario esteso al 31 Ottobre 2046) e accessibilità universale certificata ISO/IEC 40500:2012 (WCAG 2.2 Livello AAA) e Direttiva UE 2019/882 per utenti ipovedenti . Interoperable (Interoperabile): Integrazione nativa di ontologie semantiche basate su standard W3C Schema.org, JSON-LD, Dublin Core (ISO 15836:2009) e trilinguismo lineare attivo (IT, EN, FR) per l'interfacciamento con il Portafoglio Europeo di Identità Digitale (EUDI Wallet) e le Autorità di Vigilanza Europee (ESA) . Reusable (Riusabile): Tracciabilità crittografica rigorosa e immodificabile a entropia nulla ( $H = 0.0000$ ), corredata da licenza di citazione accademica (CC BY 4.0) e da riserva esplicita contro l'estrazione massiva non autorizzata e il data scraping per l'addestramento di modelli di intelligenza artificiale generativa (LLM) . 3. summary: Code, processed results and literature corpus for the article "Learning what percolation already computes: a critical review of deep learning for influential spreader identification" by Hao Liu, Xiaojie Zong, Jie Chen, Jianyu Xiong, Qiao Ke, Nan Li, Xing Li, Xiaofeng Luo and Yi-Cheng Zhang (submitted to Artificial Intelligence Review, 2026). The deposit contains: the analysis code (Python with Numba, PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric): the bond-percolation estimator of SIR influence for all nodes at once, the nested sweep over transmission rates, the epidemic percolation network for general recovery probabilities, the message-passing estimator, twelve classical centralities, re-implementations of learned spreader-ranking models (RCNN, InfGCN, a Transformer, GraphSAGE, GIN and GAT), and the benchmark, validation and timing scripts; raw and aggregated results, and per-network caches with the near-exact reference influence of every node, the literature-style ground truths (two replicates of 1000 SIR runs per seed) and all estimates; the literature corpus of the systematic review: OpenAlex records (metadata and screening flags, without abstracts), the 120 screened records, their manual coding and the list of included studies; the scripts that produce the numbers, tables and figures of the article. The public networks are not redistributed; code/data.py downloads them from Netzschleuder, SNAP and the Network Repository. README.md describes how the zip parts fit together and how to reproduce the results.
title: Code and data for: Learning what percolation already computes: a critical review of deep learning for influential spreader identification

The deposit contains: the analysis code (Python with Numba, PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric): the bond-percolation estimator of SIR influence for all nodes at once, the nested sweep over transmission rates, the epidemic percolation network for general recovery probabilities, the message-passing estimator, twelve classical centralities, re-implementations of learned spreader-ranking models (RCNN, InfGCN, a Transformer, GraphSAGE, GIN and GAT), and the benchmark, validation and timing scripts; raw and aggregated results, and per-network caches with the near-exact reference influence of every node, the literature-style ground truths (two replicates of 1000 SIR runs per seed) and all estimates; the literature corpus of the systematic review: OpenAlex records (metadata and screening flags, without abstracts), the 120 screened records, their manual coding and the list of included studies; the scripts that produce the numbers, tables and figures of the article. The public networks are not redistributed; code/data.py downloads them from Netzschleuder, SNAP and the Network Repository. README.md describes how the zip parts fit together and how to reproduce the results.

summary: This dataset accompanies the article “Spatial Spillovers and Nonlinear Determinants of PM2.5 in the European Union: A Hybrid Spatial Econometric and Machine Learning Approach” (Chovancová & Petruška). It contains a balanced panel of 27 EU member states for 2000–2020 (567 country-year observations) with PM2.5 exposure and eight candidate determinants (energy intensity, renewable energy share, Human Development Index, urbanization, population density, industrial value added, vehicle ownership and consumption-based CO2 emissions). The series are compiled from the World Bank World Development Indicators, Our World in Data and Eurostat; sources and definitions are given in the data dictionary. Vehicle ownership has 12 missing observations. The package also includes the spatial weights matrix (inverse great-circle distance between capital cities), capital coordinates, Stata code for the random forest, SHAP and partial dependence analysis and for the Moran test for spatial dependence, and Python code for permutation Moran’s I and Lagrange multiplier tests. See README.md for contents and instructions.

summary: Added palomar check reports a Challenge or Solution module root a dependency shadows (#405; #404): when the top-level root of a comparator configuration's challenge_module or solution_module is also a top-level R.lean or R/ of a dependency's source tree, the error gap challenge.module_root_shadowed or solution.module_root_shadowed (Palomar's own code). Still offline: each dependency lake-manifest.json pins is read from its .lake/packages/<name> checkout only at the pinned revision (a path dependency inside the repository from the commit), at its root and each literal srcDir . A dependency not read is named in not_checked , and a bare Challenge , Solution or Main root is then the warn gap challenge.module_root_generic or solution.module_root_generic ; when every dependency was read, not_checked drops the shadowing clause. receipt systemd --run --contracts-preflight and receipt slurm --contracts-preflight compare every comparator configuration before receipt work (#409; LO-20261030-04). They run the contracts-only diagnostic ( comparator check --contracts-only ) before the unit is created, or before the job is submitted (a receipt slurm mode of its own, [--repo DIR] , exit 0/1). A configuration that differs, a configured module that is not built (the refusal names the lake build to run) and a diagnostic that cannot run refuse, and nothing is run or written. A match prints a check line and is never part of the receipt; --json carries contracts_preflight . docs/receipts.md gains "Receipt order: the comparator receipt first" ( comparator-receipt refuses untracked files, which include a lower-tier receipt's sidecars under .lean-receipts/ ) and "Contracts preflight". Changed comparator check --contracts-only names a let kept on one side (#408; LO-20261030-04): when the first differing subterm of a type or value is a let on one side only (a Challenge keeping a let alias that the Solution's statement unfolds, or the reverse), the hint says that the two are definitionally equal but lake comparator compares the stored terms, and how to write them alike. Display only: the verdict, counts and exit code are unchanged. docs/comparator.md gains "A let kept on one side" and "Before receipt work" (build the configured modules and run the contracts-only diagnostic before launching receipt systemd or receipt slurm ); docs/how-to.md and the two receipt command pages point to it. page --write no longer writes lean-pkg-binding.yaml (#410; LO-20261030-05). On a gated package whose docs-only opt-in is only in the registry record, it used to write the file into the working tree. The file is a build input: added after the gated commit it unbinds the current receipts, so it never belongs in the documentation commit, and a renderer client could miss the side effect. page --write now prints the move as deferred advice (run lean-pkg update NAME --write-binding-file and commit the file on its own right before the next verify run). --json gains outputs[] (the files of this documentation commit) and deferred[] (the migration), and binding_file keeps its keys with state: deferred . page --write --write-binding-file writes the file as before. The registry-route step and its WARN: deprecated line are unchanged. Fixed doctor --upgrade-from no longer reads a wrapped help-text line as an option of the command (#411). It read each command's options from the help goldens and counted any indented line that began with a --flag , so a continuation line starting with a --flag mention became an option. The 0.23.0 to 0.24.0 delta listed a nonexistent receipt slurm --contracts-only , and six older phantoms ( new --license-spdx , --format on receipt comparator and receipt slurm , repo --fresh-repo , lean-pkg --yes , verify --regate ) had cancelled out. Only argparse's option lines, at exactly two spaces, are read now. A test checks every option it reads against the CLI parser. A lake-manifest.json package name that Lake writes esc
title: lean-pkg: a registry and trust gate for Lean 4 formalization packages

A dependency not read is named in not_checked , and a bare Challenge , Solution or Main root is then the warn gap challenge.module_root_generic or solution.module_root_generic ; when every dependency was read, not_checked drops the shadowing clause. receipt systemd --run --contracts-preflight and receipt slurm --contracts-preflight compare every comparator configuration before receipt work (#409; LO-20261030-04). They run the contracts-only diagnostic ( comparator check --contracts-only ) before the unit is created, or before the job is submitted (a receipt slurm mode of its own, [--repo DIR] , exit 0/1). A configuration that differs, a configured module that is not built (the refusal names the lake build to run) and a diagnostic that cannot run refuse, and nothing is run or written. A match prints a check line and is never part of the receipt; --json carries contracts_preflight . docs/receipts.md gains "Receipt order: the comparator receipt first" ( comparator-receipt refuses untracked files, which include a lower-tier receipt's sidecars under .lean-receipts/ ) and "Contracts preflight". Changed comparator check --contracts-only names a let kept on one side (#408; LO-20261030-04): when the first differing subterm of a type or value is a let on one side only (a Challenge keeping a let alias that the Solution's statement unfolds, or the reverse), the hint says that the two are definitionally equal but lake comparator compares the stored terms, and how to write them alike. Display only: the verdict, counts and exit code are unchanged. docs/comparator.md gains "A let kept on one side" and "Before receipt work" (build the configured modules and run the contracts-only diagnostic before launching receipt systemd or receipt slurm ); docs/how-to.md and the two receipt command pages point to it. page --write no longer writes lean-pkg-binding.yaml (#410; LO-20261030-05). On a gated package whose docs-only opt-in is only in the registry record, it used to write the file into the working tree. The file is a build input: added after the gated commit it unbinds the current receipts, so it never belongs in the documentation commit, and a renderer client could miss the side effect. page --write now prints the move as deferred advice (run lean-pkg update NAME --write-binding-file and commit the file on its own right before the next verify run). --json gains outputs[] (the files of this documentation commit) and deferred[] (the migration), and binding_file keeps its keys with state: deferred . page --write --write-binding-file writes the file as before. The registry-route step and its WARN: deprecated line are unchanged. Fixed doctor --upgrade-from no longer reads a wrapped help-text line as an option of the command (#411). It read each command's options from the help goldens and counted any indented line that began with a --flag , so a continuation line starting with a --flag mention became an option. The 0.23.0 to 0.24.0 delta listed a nonexistent receipt slurm --contracts-only , and six older phantoms ( new --license-spdx , --format on receipt comparator and receipt slurm , repo --fresh-repo , lean-pkg --yes , verify --regate ) had cancelled out. Only argparse's option lines, at exactly two spaces, are read now. A test checks every option it reads against the CLI parser. A lake-manifest.json package name that Lake writes esc

summary: Abstract: Classical inferential statistics and p-value hypothesis testing in healthcare big data repositories suffer from severe structural limitations, notably p-hacking, asymptotic N-bias, and the frequent violation of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumptions due to intra-patient longitudinal dependencies, hospital clustering, and epidemiological shockwaves. To overcome these failures, we introduce an Inverse Breakpoint Analysis, a scale-invariant, physics-inspired metrological audit framework. Our analysis treats discrete clinical event counts not as abstract probabilities, but as physical informational mass. Grounded in Garwood exact discrete limits and Wilson-Hilferty approximations, the framework extends our previous work on stress testing indices for Big health data and establishes three rigorous thresholds: a pure mass saturation limit, a baseline tolerance band, and a structural signal threshold. Through the use of these three parameters, our inverse break-point analysis eliminates false-positive artifacts induced by massive repository sizes while preventing under-powering in small cohorts. Ultimately, the framework demonstrates that percentage-based thresholds are kinematic artifacts of scale, whereas absolute excess discrete mass serves as the sole physical invariant for healthcare data validation. We validated this approach with numerous illustrative examples.
title: Inverse Breakpoint Analysis: A Scale-Invariant Physics-Inspired Metrological Audit for Sanitary Big Data

summary: When a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model does not fit in GPU memory, batch-1 decoding is dominated by copying expert weights from host memory. Cache-aware routing reduces these copies by biasing the router toward resident experts, but combined with asynchronous prefetching it makes the model's outputs depend on transfer timing, so a harness that does not simulate that timing no longer evaluates the deployed model. We propose prefetch-steered routing (PSR): routing conditions on a deterministic logical cache, into which at most n experts predicted by the next layer's router are inserted per layer and token; physical copies affect only latency. On OLMoE-1B-7B with 50% and 25% of experts resident on an RTX 4090, PSR decodes 2.2-2.3x faster than exact routing with LRU and 25-30% faster than the Cache-Prior operating point, with mean benchmark differences of +0.1 and +0.5 points (95% lower bounds -0.8 and -0.3). In greedy generation its lead over Cache-Prior depends on the workload and reverses on HumanEval at 50% residency. On Moonlight-16B-A3B, PSR is 1.9x faster than exact routing with LRU at 37.5% residency and, at the latency of Cache-Prior, significantly better on three of eight benchmarks. On Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, where copies are cheap relative to computation, PSR keeps its advantage over Cache-Prior on the likelihood benchmarks but not its speed. Distillation-trained gates did not help. Speculative decoding with block-level expert selection was slower than PSR with a 1B autoregressive drafter on OLMoE, but with a block drafter on Qwen3.6 it was 2.1-2.9x faster than any autoregressive configuration with at most its GPU memory on the 64 prompts we timed.
title: Prefetch-Steered Routing: Deterministic Cache-Aware Expert Selection for Offloaded Mixture-of-Experts Decoding

summary: On million-node graphs, the memory wall arrives before the compute wall: a GNN that never fits in VRAM cannot deliver the all-node inference its accuracy promises. The standard remedy, pruning, has always been an accuracy tax - paid once and never refunded. DPR refuses this framing. Its central insight is that the mask that shrinks training can also scaffold recovery: one compact node set bounds both computations of graph learning, serving as the encoder's training graph and, at inference, as the anchor from which a sparse structure-aware decoder rebuilds every pruned node (double-layer sparsification). The order is inverted - prune for efficiency, then reconstruct for accuracy - and the tax is repaid: the deployed 30%-budget model trains in 1,450 MiB of peak memory on one 6 GB GPU and recovers 96.9% of its dense-reconstruction reference, beating a same-GPU rerun of the edge-sparsification baseline DSpar by +1.36 pp at 50.1% lower peak training memory; against the same-protocol full-batch no-prune encoder the deployed point pays a measured 2.64 pp accuracy tax for a 2.8x smaller training footprint. Pruning without reconstruction leaves the encoder at 0.378 within the same 40-epoch window (Fig. 4), and all-node serving runs 46x faster than sampling-based GraphSAGE, giving up approx. 5.4 pp of test accuracy. The framework scales to a 2.45M-node production graph at 6,285 MiB of peak training memory; extended variants (long-range context, external text features, a CAN-bus application) are reported as extensions and do not compete with the deployed method, and the 41.8%-budget M4 point, scored on a coarsened super-node graph with its own split, is reported separately rather than compared with the original-node baselines. DPR thus turns aggressive node pruning from an accuracy tax into a safe training accelerator for VRAM-limited all-node inference.
title: Decoupled Prune-and-Reconstruct: Training on a Compact Core with Double-Layer Sparsification

summary: Many mathematical research agents focus on solving problems with fixed statements. However, conjecture research, especially in applied mathematics, may require revising candidate questions or conclusions as investigation proceeds, coupling problem formulation with proof development. We present PACE, a research-proof agent that supports this process through a structured research loop that selects mathematical objectives and develops or challenges candidate mechanisms. The whole prover constructs proofs from these mechanisms, and an independent verifier checks them against the original target. Evidence-tracking memory stores assumptions and dependencies arising during research and marks evidence for revalidation when a candidate or condition changes. This memory supports task-specific context composition that keeps checked premises, exploratory material and unresolved obligations distinct. To evaluate proof construction and conjecture research, we introduce ResearchProofBench, an applied-mathematics benchmark focused on optimization, comprising 51 known-proof tasks with 331 hidden checkpoints under historical abstract access and six open-problem cases. The known-proof tasks assess reconstruction of published results, while the open-problem cases assess mathematical investigation and proof development. On the 51 known-proof tasks, PACE achieves an aggregate Proof Score of 75.16 and completes 20 proofs. In conjecture research, PACE develops conditional results, with its submissions receiving higher review scores than the compared baselines.
title: PACE: Research Proving Agent for Adaptive Conjecture Exploration

summary: Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems (MAS) rely on role-specific prompts and execution models to solve complex tasks collaboratively. However, prompt optimization typically keeps model assignments fixed, leaving differences in role requirements and their associated inference costs outside the search. We present UniMASO, a Unified framework for heterogeneous Multi-Agent System Optimization through the joint adaptation of prompts and model assignments. UniMASO evaluates candidate updates through local, downstream, and global feedback, using cost-aware Pareto search to retain useful quality-cost trade-offs. Topology-aware co-evolution then coordinates these updates according to agent roles and dependencies. Cross-level trajectory memory further supplies historical successes and failures to guide subsequent optimization. Experiments on five benchmarks and five execution topologies show that UniMASO achieves competitive task performance at substantially lower deployment cost than the strongest homogeneous configurations. Under centralized execution, it improves the average score from 69.79 to 70.40 while reducing token-weighted deployment cost by 85.2% relative to DeepSeek-V4-Pro with MASPO. These results support joint prompt-model adaptation as an effective approach to efficient multi-agent collaboration. The code is available at https://github.com/Achilles008/UniMASO_main.
title: Not Every Agent Needs the Strongest Model: Unified Prompt-Model Optimization for Heterogeneous LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

direction_title: Rowan / BBC1 protein structural confidence vs experimental stability falsification [CONTROL]
summary: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly automate complex tasks, with multi-agent systems seeking further performance gains through specialization and collaboration. However, distributing work across agents does not automatically yield complementary contributions, and inter-agent dependencies can turn local errors into task failure. To address these challenges, we propose AutoSwarm, a multi-agent framework for collaborative problem solving. Collaboration formation jointly defines responsibility boundaries and conditions for acceptance and downstream use, grounding capability allocation in contributions that other agents can assess and integrate toward a shared objective. Execution coordination couples agents' local progress through a shared state, using dependencies and supervisory relationships to govern agent activation, result handoffs, and integration while adapting subsequent actions to review feedback and emerging blockers. Experiments spanning long-horizon programming, interactive planning, and professional financial analysis demonstrate AutoSwarm's advantages over single-agent baselines and existing multi-agent frameworks. Source code is available at https://github.com/HKUDS/AutoSwarm.
title: AutoSwarm: Automating Agent Swarms

summary: Research artifact for the journal article Fresh on Paper, Reused in Code: Static Detection of Hidden Key Reuse in Cancelable Biometric Systems (submitted to the Journal of Information Security and Applications). The archive contains a non-executing Python static analyzer that traces record-dependent key provenance to reviewed BioHash, IoM-GRP and PolyProtect protection calls and reports reuse , conditional_fresh or unknown ; the internally authored source-case benchmarks with expected labels and Bandit outputs; analyzer development and confirmation results (v1-v3, intraprocedural baseline, branch counterexample and regression); experiment protocols and configurations; and aggregate results of the matched key-policy remediation and utility studies. summary: Early-warning models in learning analytics can identify learners at risk of failure or withdrawal, but the resulting alerts are often only weakly connected to inspectable learning evidence. The twin is updated at temporal checkpoints by replaying learning traces and assessment records, and it serves both as a feature-extraction substrate and as an explanation-grounding substrate. Predictive features are derived through graph-mediated queries, while features, attributions, alerts, evidence items, and raw records are represented as queryable graph entities. summary: Self-improving AI systems can revise the designs that govern their own behavior. Yet existing approaches center improvement on selected parent agents and their evolutionary experience, leaving the broader population largely underused. We identify a substantial gap between population coverage (i.e., the tasks solved by at least one evolved variant) and the performance of the best individual agent. This gap shows that useful capabilities and diagnostic evidence emerge across the population without being consolidated into its leading agents. These observations motivate the view from nowhere, a principle for agent evolution: an agent should be improved by interpreting its behavior through population-wide patterns of success, failure, and prior self-modification. We instantiate this principle as Population-Centered Evolution (PCE). PCE distils task records and modification histories from the population into a population block, which captures recurring failures, complementary successes, and the effects of previously attempted modifications to guide improvements to a selected parent's harness. Under matched models, initial harnesses, and evolution schedules, PCE achieves 72.1% success on SWE-bench Verified and 96.7% on Polyglot, improving over a strong group-evolution baseline by 3.2 and 5.9 percentage points. In our evaluation, PCE reduces the gap between population coverage and best-agent performance by one-third on SWE-bench and closes it on Polyglot. These results suggest that treating the population as evidence--not merely as candidates for selection--provides a complementary principle for agent evolution.

summary: Perceiving human body motion is critical for multimodal systems that understand and assist people. We evaluate 37 leading closed-source, open-source, and specialized egocentric MLLMs, complemented by an extensive human evaluation. We find that humans also find this task difficult from video alone (68.5% accuracy), yet clearly outperform the strongest MLLM (Qwen3.6-27B), which reaches 50.0% zero-shot accuracy. By identifying common failure modes and missing capabilities in current MLLMs, we hope SOMA will inspire future research on body-motion understanding and multimodal reasoning. summary: QIGONG BREATHING AND INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE NEUROFEEDBACK COUPLING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English Research Working Edition that constructs a falsifiable, explicitly nonclinical research program joining measured breathing tasks, cardiorespiratory and EEG feedback, and isolated microscale actuator surrogates. The central problem is not whether breathing changes heart-rate variability - that has established ordinary physiological explanations - but whether a proposed feedback architecture adds independently measurable predictive or benchtop-control value after breathing rate, phase, expectancy, ordinary cardiorespiratory dynamics, sensor calibration, stimulus timing and strong conventional controllers have been fairly matched. The primary hypothesis is deliberately narrow. A prospective factorial design separates a preregistered breathing condition from an isolated, non-human phantom-drive condition. Its interaction term, order effects, washout, hierarchical sampling units, pressure-related mechanisms and full-episode denominators are subjected to masked scheduling, matched sham sensory cues, covariance-aware uncertainty and independent laboratory reconstruction. Any apparent signal explained by paced breathing or cue entrainment is treated as a legitimate negative result. A bench interaction is not evidence of physiological effects from actual acupuncture in a person. Thirty mathematically differentiated research plates address factorial contrasts, hierarchical estimands, respiratory sinus arrhythmia, ECG event genealogy, pressure-respiration transfer, spectral coherence, lag and phase, multiple comparisons, uncertainty covariance, causal identification, feedback latency, safe-state projection, isolated charge and thermal constraints, abstention and provenance. Across 82 chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations, the book examines operational breathing definitions, reference instruments, EEG and ECG artifacts, blinded feedback protocols, mechanical and electrical phantoms, strong ordinary competitors, statistics, safety vetoes and reproducible handoff. Two hundred full-page Research Gates place their complete falsifiable research question in large deep-navy type, followed by an independently measurable outcome, adverse experiment, conventional physical rival and stopping rule. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose distinct successor objects ranging from calibration bridges and sham credibility tests to independent hardware vetoes, covariance sentinels, multisite reference capsules and protected null-result archives. An accompanying Excel index links formulas, chapters, Gates, candidate objects, citations and explicit evidence limitations. This work reports no executed integrated experiments, in-human needling, electrical stimulation, clinical efficacy, diagnosis or regulatory authorization. Its three STARLI mother-volume DOIs establish author research-method ancestry. Thirteen separately identified external research and metrology DOIs support established measurement, breathing physiology, neurofeedback reporting, uncertainty and statistical methodology, not the novel combined hypothesis. The 777-page layout, formula-clearance checks and 200 Gate color checks were automated; recurring editorial phrasing remains and full independent scientific peer review has not taken place. summary: BIOELECTRIC FEEDBACK AND PERSONALIZED INTELLIGENT ACUPUNCTURE CONTROL AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page prospective nonclinical research monograph on the boundary between measured bioelectric variability, personalized feedback algorithms, and genuinely verified safe closed-loop operation on inert phantoms and isolated bench hardware. Its primary question is whether a controller calibrated on limited reference data retains a meaningful improvement for entirely unseen simulated individuals while meeting hard, independently witnessed limits. The governing design separates physiological sensing, identification of individual model parameters, selection of feedback commands, and observed physical outcomes. The inherited objective is corrected to a unit-consistent normalized tracking loss and separately measured bench-output burden; no mathematical optimum can compensate a failed hardware veto, force cap, thermal boundary, or missing permission record. A synthetic dummy-output budget is explicitly not a clinical stimulation dose or therapeutic recommendation. Thirty differentiated mathematical plates explore covariance-aware metrology, personal and hierarchical system identification, robust model predictive control, posterior coverage, safe-set feasibility, population shift, abstention, actuator latency, thermal loading, physical isolation, state-space reachability, distributional tail risk and independent requalification. Each plate states construction assumptions, native units, blind tests, stop conditions and a crosswalk to relevant chapters and successor gates. Eighty-two chapters, each with five separately paginated studies, develop electrode and reference calibration, timebase reliability, individual parameter uncertainty, adversarial new-person transfer, fair PID and classical MPC comparisons, closed-loop constraints, sham feedback, safety engineering and handoff to an unrelated laboratory. Two hundred full-page Research Gates are designed as distinctly falsifiable future entry points, including blind reconstruction, strong conventional rivals and external adversarial continuation. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose different metrology tools, decision records, baseline devices or smaller successor theories that can survive disproof of the larger control claim. The three author mother-volume version DOIs are M1 10.5281/zenodo.23480803, M2 10.5281/zenodo.23486020 and M3 10.5281/zenodo.23318840. Separately identified published external DOI studies on neural decoding, population generalization, system identification, control and neurostimulation provide context only: none demonstrates this F47 integrated apparatus. This is a Research Working Edition, not an executed laboratory study, clinical trial, review approval or evidence of therapeutic benefit. Future human stimulation, puncture, clinical research and patient-facing equipment require their own independent regulatory and ethics program. summary: At the start of 1984 Britain still had a large deep coal industry; by the end of 1994 almost all of it had gone, and the last deep mine closed in 2015. Do the towns that grew up around the pits still look different from other towns, and does it matter when their pit closed? I compile a list of 196 deep mines working at the start of 1984 from the Northern Mine Research Society's tables of National Coal Board collieries and Wikipedia's colliery lists, with closure years and locations from OpenStreetMap, Wikidata and OS Open Names. 167 (85%) closed by the end of 1994, with a peak of 32 in 1985. Linking the pits to the ONS built-up areas of 2022, I find 209 pit towns of 2,000 to 100,000 people in England and Wales. Compared with towns of the same size in the same region that had no pit, in Census 2021 they have 2.0 percentage points more adults long-term sick or disabled (a comparison-town median of 2.9%), 3.2 points more adults inactive for reasons other than retirement or study, 6.5 points more in routine or semi-routine work, 8.0 points fewer in managerial or professional work and about £5,900 a year lower mean household income, but the same share in work. Towns with older collieries show about half the gap. Among pit towns, the year the last pit closed makes no clear difference. Because the coalfields differed from other places long before 1984 and no earlier baseline is used, these are associations, not effects of the closures. Interactive version: https://tristan-hotham.github.io/pit-closures/ . Data and code: https://github.com/Tristan-Hotham/pit-closures . Blog post: https://blog.tristanhotham.com/2026/10/28/pit-closures/ .
title: Did the Pits Closing Still Show? Britain's Coalfield Towns, 1984 to 2021

summary: Fine-grained visual perception remains a bottleneck during post-training of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), as perceptual errors can constrain gains from reasoning-focused optimization. Although image-caption pre-training improves perception, its influence can weaken as subsequent stages change data mixtures and objectives. Continuing caption supervision during post-training is challenging because subjective, information-dense descriptions complicate verifiable reward design. We present PerceptRL, which strengthens perception at two complementary levels. Perception RL uses a multi-agent pipeline to extract verified errors from dense image captions and convert the corresponding visual facts into QA pairs with fixed answer labels and rule-based rewards. Chain QA links correlated errors, while multiple-choice QA combines unrelated errors. A specialized route targets high-error domains with tailored verification, and a domain-agnostic general route covers errors beyond these domains. Perception Agentic RL addresses fine-grained and dense cases unresolved by single-turn Perception RL through multi-turn inspection with visual tools. We observe coordinate drift even in models trained to use tools, where incorrect crops or annotations distort evidence and propagate errors. Coordinate Injection corrects spatial operations in cold-start trajectories, while a grounding-aware process reward supervises intermediate spatial fidelity alongside final-answer correctness. Training proceeds through shared cold-start SFT, single-turn Perception RL, and multi-turn Perception Agentic RL. Across seven benchmarks under a shared tool-use protocol, PerceptRL achieves 71.6% average accuracy, surpassing the base model with the same tools and the strongest evaluated frontier VLM by 15.7 and 5.2 percentage points, respectively.
title: PerceptRL: Making Visual Perception Rewardable in MLLMs from Answers to Interactions

summary: Electric vehicle (EV) charging stations integrating photovoltaic (PV) generation, battery storage, and bidirectional grid exchange must coordinate access to limited chargers with energy supply while considering both energy cost and carbon emissions. This paper proposes a solver-free greedy heuristic (SFGH) for dynamic vehicle scheduling (VS) and a twin delayed deep deterministic policy gradient (TD3) controller for carbon-aware energy dispatch (ED). SFGH assigns EVs according to reductions in service delays, and TD3 controls battery operation to balance energy costs and carbon emissions while meeting the resulting charging demand. The model allows both PV and battery exports, accounting for export revenue and carbon credits. Simulations on year-long case studies show that SFGH--TD3 achieves the lowest accumulated service delay, energy cost, and carbon emissions among the evaluated heuristic and multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (DRL) configurations.
title: Electric Vehicle Scheduling and Carbon-Aware Energy Dispatch for Charging Stations

summary: Evaluating natural language explanations in recommender systems is essential for fostering user trust, transparency, and engagement. However, existing evaluation approaches like human evaluations, while accurate, are resource-intensive and impractical at the scale required by modern recommendation platforms. Also, automated methods using single-agent LLMs suffer from prompt sensitivity and inconsistent outputs. To address these challenges, we propose MAREval, a structured multi-agent framework for evaluating recommendation explanations using large language models. MAREval orchestrates (i) a planner agent that uses a novel Chain of Debate (CoD) prompting strategy to coordinate agent roles and enforce logically consistent evaluation plans; (ii) a moderator agent that regulates discussions by mitigating prompt drift; and (iii) an arbitrator agent that aggregates outputs from multiple evaluation rounds and (iv) a Monte Carlo sampling method, improving robustness and alignment with human judgment. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on both public (TopicalChat) and proprietary recommendation datasets, demonstrating that MAREval outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Comprehensive experiments on a public benchmark and a proprietary e-commerce dataset show that MAREval improves alignment with human judgments over strong singleand multi-agent baselines. Stability analyses indicate substantially lower variability across repeated trials. In a large human-annotation gate, MAREval meets production quality thresholds where prior evaluators fall short, and online A/B testing demonstrates statistically significant improvements in engagement and revenue metrics. These results establish MAREval as a scalable and reliable solution for human-aligned evaluation of recommendation explanations in real-world systems
title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations
