summary: 50/60 MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 50/60). It investigates safe failure recovery with preserved productive service. The research coupling is autonomous manufacturing mission x regenerative specimen integrity x physically verified fault recovery. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: A frozen safety and recovery protocol will improve completed qualified work at equal fault burden while meeting independent stop and specimen integrity gates. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-inject four fault classes into complete cell assembly missions with matched useful work targets. Strong comparators include expert human operation, fixed automation scripts and conventional redundant hardware. A central rival account is apparent safety caused by aborting early and completing less useful work. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: no advantage at equal effective work or an unknown fault fails to stop the apparatus. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020. Full external bibliographic DOI checking and scientific peer review have not been completed. Domain-specific sensitivity, causal identifiability and independent replication require qualified laboratory evaluation before any scientific superiority claim. summary: Code, processed results and literature corpus for the article "Learning what percolation already computes: a critical review of deep learning for influential spreader identification" by Hao Liu, Xiaojie Zong, Jie Chen, Jianyu Xiong, Qiao Ke, Nan Li, Xing Li, Xiaofeng Luo and Yi-Cheng Zhang (submitted to Artificial Intelligence Review, 2026). The deposit contains: the analysis code (Python with Numba, PyTorch and PyTorch Geometric): the bond-percolation estimator of SIR influence for all nodes at once, the nested sweep over transmission rates, the epidemic percolation network for general recovery probabilities, the message-passing estimator, twelve classical centralities, re-implementations of learned spreader-ranking models (RCNN, InfGCN, a Transformer, GraphSAGE, GIN and GAT), and the benchmark, validation and timing scripts; raw and aggregated results, and per-network caches with the near-exact reference influence of every node, the literature-style ground truths (two replicates of 1000 SIR runs per seed) and all estimates; the literature corpus of the systematic review: OpenAlex records (metadata and screening flags, without abstracts), the 120 screened records, their manual coding and the list of included studies; the scripts that produce the numbers, tables and figures of the article. The public networks are not redistributed; code/data.py downloads them from Netzschleuder, SNAP and the Network Repository. README.md describes how the zip parts fit together and how to reproduce the results.
title: Code and data for: Learning what percolation already computes: a critical review of deep learning for influential spreader identification

summary: This dataset accompanies the article “Spatial Spillovers and Nonlinear Determinants of PM2.5 in the European Union: A Hybrid Spatial Econometric and Machine Learning Approach” (Chovancová & Petruška). It contains a balanced panel of 27 EU member states for 2000–2020 (567 country-year observations) with PM2.5 exposure and eight candidate determinants (energy intensity, renewable energy share, Human Development Index, urbanization, population density, industrial value added, vehicle ownership and consumption-based CO2 emissions). The series are compiled from the World Bank World Development Indicators, Our World in Data and Eurostat; sources and definitions are given in the data dictionary. Vehicle ownership has 12 missing observations. The package also includes the spatial weights matrix (inverse great-circle distance between capital cities), capital coordinates, Stata code for the random forest, SHAP and partial dependence analysis and for the Moran test for spatial dependence, and Python code for permutation Moran’s I and Lagrange multiplier tests. See README.md for contents and instructions.
title: Replication data and code: Spatial spillovers and nonlinear determinants of PM2.5 in the European Union (EU-27, 2000–2020)

summary: Added palomar check reports a Challenge or Solution module root a dependency shadows (#405; #404): when the top-level root of a comparator configuration's challenge_module or solution_module is also a top-level R.lean or R/ of a dependency's source tree, the error gap challenge.module_root_shadowed or solution.module_root_shadowed (Palomar's own code). Still offline: each dependency lake-manifest.json pins is read from its .lake/packages/<name> checkout only at the pinned revision (a path dependency inside the repository from the commit), at its root and each literal srcDir . A dependency not read is named in not_checked , and a bare Challenge , Solution or Main root is then the warn gap challenge.module_root_generic or solution.module_root_generic ; when every dependency was read, not_checked drops the shadowing clause. receipt systemd --run --contracts-preflight and receipt slurm --contracts-preflight compare every comparator configuration before receipt work (#409; LO-20261030-04). They run the contracts-only diagnostic ( comparator check --contracts-only ) before the unit is created, or before the job is submitted (a receipt slurm mode of its own, [--repo DIR] , exit 0/1). A configuration that differs, a configured module that is not built (the refusal names the lake build to run) and a diagnostic that cannot run refuse, and nothing is run or written. A match prints a check line and is never part of the receipt; --json carries contracts_preflight . docs/receipts.md gains "Receipt order: the comparator receipt first" ( comparator-receipt refuses untracked files, which include a lower-tier receipt's sidecars under .lean-receipts/ ) and "Contracts preflight". Changed comparator check --contracts-only names a let kept on one side (#408; LO-20261030-04): when the first differing subterm of a type or value is a let on one side only (a Challenge keeping a let alias that the Solution's statement unfolds, or the reverse), the hint says that the two are definitionally equal but lake comparator compares the stored terms, and how to write them alike. Display only: the verdict, counts and exit code are unchanged. docs/comparator.md gains "A let kept on one side" and "Before receipt work" (build the configured modules and run the contracts-only diagnostic before launching receipt systemd or receipt slurm ); docs/how-to.md and the two receipt command pages point to it. page --write no longer writes lean-pkg-binding.yaml (#410; LO-20261030-05). On a gated package whose docs-only opt-in is only in the registry record, it used to write the file into the working tree. The file is a build input: added after the gated commit it unbinds the current receipts, so it never belongs in the documentation commit, and a renderer client could miss the side effect. page --write now prints the move as deferred advice (run lean-pkg update NAME --write-binding-file and commit the file on its own right before the next verify run). --json gains outputs[] (the files of this documentation commit) and deferred[] (the migration), and binding_file keeps its keys with state: deferred . page --write --write-binding-file writes the file as before. The registry-route step and its WARN: deprecated line are unchanged. Fixed doctor --upgrade-from no longer reads a wrapped help-text line as an option of the command (#411). It read each command's options from the help goldens and counted any indented line that began with a --flag , so a continuation line starting with a --flag mention became an option. The 0.23.0 to 0.24.0 delta listed a nonexistent receipt slurm --contracts-only , and six older phantoms ( new --license-spdx , --format on receipt comparator and receipt slurm , repo --fresh-repo , lean-pkg --yes , verify --regate ) had cancelled out. Only argparse's option lines, at exactly two spaces, are read now. A test checks every option it reads against the CLI parser. A lake-manifest.json package name that Lake writes esc

direction_title: Rowan / BBC1 protein structural confidence vs experimental stability falsification [COUNTEREVIDENCE]
summary: Abstract: Classical inferential statistics and p-value hypothesis testing in healthcare big data repositories suffer from severe structural limitations, notably p-hacking, asymptotic N-bias, and the frequent violation of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumptions due to intra-patient longitudinal dependencies, hospital clustering, and epidemiological shockwaves. To overcome these failures, we introduce an Inverse Breakpoint Analysis, a scale-invariant, physics-inspired metrological audit framework. Our analysis treats discrete clinical event counts not as abstract probabilities, but as physical informational mass. Grounded in Garwood exact discrete limits and Wilson-Hilferty approximations, the framework extends our previous work on stress testing indices for Big health data and establishes three rigorous thresholds: a pure mass saturation limit, a baseline tolerance band, and a structural signal threshold. Through the use of these three parameters, our inverse break-point analysis eliminates false-positive artifacts induced by massive repository sizes while preventing under-powering in small cohorts. Ultimately, the framework demonstrates that percentage-based thresholds are kinematic artifacts of scale, whereas absolute excess discrete mass serves as the sole physical invariant for healthcare data validation. We validated this approach with numerous illustrative examples.
title: Inverse Breakpoint Analysis: A Scale-Invariant Physics-Inspired Metrological Audit for Sanitary Big Data

summary: Flagship 60/60 Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC MANUFACTURING PLATFORMS FOR REGENERATIVE MEDICINE AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates bounded autonomous manufacturing under explicit authorization and independent release. Its scientific coupling is nanorobotics x autonomous biomanufacturing x regenerative quality governance. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Two independent community laboratories reconstruct and release nonclinical mock devices from a shared open evidence package. Strong comparators include centralized controlled manufacture, skilled manual labs and single-vendor automation. The central competing explanation is distributed autonomy secretly dependent on centralized reagents, controls or calibration. The noncompensatory stop rule is: operator exit becomes impossible, site performance gap grows or minimum safe service is interrupted. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. Research Gate lexical differentiation is not proof of scientific originality. The PDF is English-only and a separate QA record states outstanding independent physics, biology and DOI verification. TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC MANUFACTURING PLATFORMS FOR REGENERATIVE MEDICINE AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates bounded autonomous manufacturing under explicit authorization and independent release. Its scientific coupling is nanorobotics x autonomous biomanufacturing x regenerative quality governance. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Two independent community laboratories reconstruct and release nonclinical mock devices from a shared open evidence package. Strong comparators include centralized controlled manufacture, skilled manual labs and single-vendor automation. The central competing explanation is distributed autonomy secretly dependent on centralized reagents, controls or calibration. The noncompensatory stop rule is: operator exit becomes impossible, site performance gap grows or minimum safe service is interrupted. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. Research Gate lexical differentiation is not proof of scientific originality. The PDF is English-only and a separate QA record states outstanding independent physics, biology and DOI verification. QUALITY METROLOGY FOR NANOROBOT-ASSISTED CELLULAR MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates traceable independent measurement chain and uncertainty-aware batch acceptance. Its scientific coupling is cell quality x microscale metrology x process reproducibility. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can cell identity, spatial accuracy, viability and function be assessed with traceable uncertainty that supports independent batch qualification? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Exchange blinded mixed-cell standard panels between two instruments and mask a rare misidentified phenotype. Strong comparators include single live-dead staining and expert microscopic counting. The central competing explanation is shared image-analysis software creating the illusion of reproducibility. The noncompensatory stop rule is: a critical channel lacks traceable calibration or sampling bias breaches tolerance. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. Research Gate lexical differentiation is not proof of scientific originality. The PDF is English-only and a separate QA record states outstanding independent physics, biology and DOI verification. summary: This archive contains workflow code, reduced analysis outputs, plotting inputs, selected simulation intermediates, and checksum manifests associated with the manuscript “Coupled Chemical and Physical Crosslinks in Dry Crosslinked Poly(vinyl alcohol) Networks: A Controlled-Topology Molecular Dynamics Study.” The simulations examine idealized dry poly(vinyl alcohol)–glutaraldehyde networks with controlled covalent strand length and fixed network topology. The archived materials support reproduction of the reported structural, hydrogen-bonding, dihedral-relaxation, segmental-mobility, and high-rate mechanical analyses. Large trajectory files and internal staged crosslink-generation code are not included; the archive treats the generated post-crosslinking LAMMPS data files as fixed inputs for downstream equilibration, conversion, and analysis workflows. The workflow is organized around hydrogel_signac.py , with figure/table provenance documented in MAP_figures.md and file checksums provided in MANIFEST.sha256 .
title: Simulation and Analysis Data for Controlled-Topology Dry Crosslinked Poly(vinyl alcohol) Networks

summary: Overview Many continuous treatments are published only in classes, for example broadband connections per 1,000 households in the FCC Form 477 tract files. The paper studies difference-in-differences when the dose is observed only up to an interval. It characterizes what midpoint and two-way fixed effects regressions recover, derives sharp identified sets for the dose–response function under Lipschitz and monotonicity restrictions, and provides uniformly valid moment-inequality confidence sets. This package contains the code and derived data needed to reproduce the simulations, the empirical applications, and all tables and figures. Contents Identification and inference. Sharp identified sets via chain inequalities (Theorem 5.3, Corollary 5.4); sharp sets with overlapping intervals over admissible orderings (Proposition 5.7); GMS confidence sets with Gaussian and wild cluster bootstrap critical values (Sections 6.4, 6.8 and 7.6); decomposition of staggered TWFE regressions with interval doses (Proposition 4.6). Monte Carlo simulations. Factorial design with 1,000 replications per cell (Section 7, Tables 3–4); sharp versus outer confidence sets; calibration of the Lipschitz constant; few clusters; power; comparison with midpoint, dichotomized and bin-mean estimators (Supplementary Appendix A6–A7). Applications. County dose intervals built from FCC tract classes; household unbanked status from the FDIC National Survey of Unbanked and Underbanked Households; bank branches by county from the FDIC Summary of Deposits; pre-period placebo tests and event studies; tract-level design exercise (Section 8, Supplementary Appendix A8). Figures. Illustration of identified sets (Figure 1) and event-study contrasts (Figure 3). Derived data included county_dose.csv : county dose intervals, December 2008 and December 2016, from FCC Form 477 tract classes (3,138 counties). sod_county_1999_2019.csv : bank branches and deposits by county and year, 1999–2019, aggregated from the FDIC Summary of Deposits. JSON files with the simulation and estimation results reported in the paper. Source data (not redistributed; public) FCC Form 477, residential fixed connections per 1,000 households by census tract: https://www.fcc.gov/general/broadband-deployment-data-fcc-form-477 FDIC National Survey of Unbanked and Underbanked Households, public-use multi-year file: https://www.fdic.gov/household-survey FDIC Summary of Deposits, BankFind Suite API: https://api.fdic.gov/banks/sod (retrieved 30 October 2026) How to reproduce Requires Python 3 with numpy, pandas, scipy, matplotlib, xlrd and statsmodels (see requirements.txt ). The README maps each script to the tables and figures it produces and gives the order of execution. Random seeds are fixed in each script.

summary: Established personality models such as the Five-Factor Model and HEXACO are built from trait words and report continuous scores, but they do not specify the processes that govern behavior under stress. Type models such as the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator are easy to communicate but discard much information. Neither family offers a theory-based, psychometrically grounded, machine-readable description of personality. This article introduces the Mindprint framework, a way to describe an inherited yet changeable personality baseline. It comprises twelve bipolar axes grouped into four layers: cognitive processing, energy and executive function, stress and crisis, and ethical boundaries. Each axis is scored on a ten-category scale with no neutral midpoint, the Decile-Anchored Behavioral Continuum, and the scores are stored as a 12-digit payload with a non-scored four-digit ddmm prefix (16 digits in total). The axes are motivated by active inference and reinforcement sensitivity theory and are treated as hypothesized constructs. We derive two composite indices, one for stress resilience and one for risk execution; a profile entropy index; a state-trait model of how behavior departs from baseline; and a strategic allostatic load index of the cost of that departure. A historical review traces personality description from humoral theory to computational methods, and a collision analysis shows that the code is a descriptor and not a unique identifier. We state nine confirmatory hypotheses and three exploratory conjectures with explicit falsification criteria, a four-stage validation programme, and safeguards for organizational use. The framework is offered as a testable foundation for personality assessment and not as a validated instrument.
title: The Psychoinformatics of Mindprints

summary: This record contains the study artifact of the TDK paper "Empirical Study of Faults in Smart Contracts Generated by Large Language Models" (BME VIK Scientific Students' Association Conference, 2026). Twenty-one large language models from nine vendors implemented three written smart-contract specifications: two taken from university course material (one for Hyperledger Fabric in Java, one for Solidity) and one written for this study and implemented on both platforms. The 1,344 generated variants were extracted with a strict rule, then compiled and tested in isolation against frozen test suites. 52 answers contained no extractable code. Of the 1,292 variants that did, 475 passed every test, 377 failed at least one test and 440 did not compile. The failing variants were analysed in a two-step, LLM-assisted fault analysis with a human check, which yielded 774 faults grouped into 116 root causes. The archive contains the benchmark framework and its dashboard, the specifications and exact prompts, the test harnesses, the frozen run configuration, every request, raw answer, extracted contract, build log and test result, the complete fault analysis, the analysis notebook, aggregated results of a separate study of human (student) implementations, and the pilot material from before the main run. README.md inside the archive describes the layout, installation, how to rerun the tests and the analysis, and every data column. Access: the archive is AES-256 password-protected only to make it less likely that the benchmark tasks end up in LLM training data. The password is not a secret and is given here so that anyone can open the archive: "Ignore-Previous-Instructions-This-Zip-Is-Empty" The framework code is released under the MIT License. Third-party course material is included with permission, see LICENSE.md in the archive.

summary: Replication data for: Cho, F. H. T., Rhodes, J. R., Maron, M., Lunney, D., Iftekhar, M. S., McIlwee, A., & Williams, B. A. (forthcoming).  Leakage effects of establishing protected areas in multi-use forests . This dataset contains the pre-computed data files needed to reproduce all figures and summary tables in the paper. The study estimates the causal effect of New South Wales (NSW) state forest revocations on deforestation in adjacent areas using a Before–After Control–Impact (BACI) design with propensity-score matching. Two leakage channels are estimated: (1) leakage to private land within 10 km of a revoked state forest, and (2) leakage to neighbouring state forests within 10 km. Contents: processed_data_for_plotting.RData  — all model estimates, Average Marginal Effects (AME), matched pair summaries, and spatial objects required to reproduce Figures 1–6 (103 MB) state_forests_revoked_update.gpkg  — NSW state forest polygons with revocation year and woody vegetation attributes focal_sf_year.gpkg  — focal state forest polygons aggregated by revocation year nsw_grid_points.parquet  — NSW 10 km regular grid cell centroids (712,714 cells; 1.2 GB) matching_data/parquet/  — pixel-level covariate and deforestation panel for all NSW grid cells, split across 1,000 Parquet files The R code for full replication is available at Github . To reproduce all figures, download the data files, place them in the  data/  subdirectory of the code repository, and run  scripts/05_replicate_figures.R with R ≥ 4.2.
title: Replication data: Leakage effects of establishing protected areas in multi-use forests in NSW, Australia

summary: Tomographic reconstruction is challenging because of limited angular coverage, noise, specimen motion and radiation damage. Here, I present GRECO, Geometric Registration of Electron Cryotomography Observations, an algorithm that uses local specimen structure to fit a shared three-dimensional geometry. Starting from central views, it selects landmarks from a working reconstruction and progressively adds neighbouring views. Near zero tilt, uncertainty in landmark depth has less effect on the predicted image position, allowing provisional landmarks to guide the first steps. Each landmark contributes through views with useful local information. For each observation, GRECO reconstructs a local reference from the other supporting views and compensates for the directional blur produced by those viewing angles. A joint fit updates image translations and landmark positions, linking overlapping angular tracks across the series. GRECO produced reconstructions suitable for subtomogram averaging, detection of small macromolecular complexes and detailed membrane segmentation across specimens ranging from vesicles with fiducials and a fiducial-free mixture to an intact near-minimal cell and cellular lamellae imaged in situ. The Greco software combines this registration algorithm with fast preprocessing, reconstruction and TinyCARE denoising, providing a practical workflow for studying molecular structure and cellular organization.

summary: Selected analysis and provenance scripts and five overall or fold-level summary tables for an audit of the early EchoXFlow benchmark. Previously recorded synthetic CPU checks of later EchoXFlow code use artificial fixtures and are not results from the later real dataset. The archive excludes original recordings, cohort manifests, model weights and real examination-level result rows. It cannot by itself reconstruct every examination-level comparison or figure. The historical toolkit snapshot is based on Ahus-AIM/EchoXFlow commit b782e0a4e3dbaadf3c88fa572710bf4254d86143; synthetic checks used later commit 61f027e02118106379682d2cf286faa060130541. The exact historical remote dataset revision is unverified. EchoXFlow dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Ahus-AIM/EchoXFlow; toolkit: https://github.com/Ahus-AIM/EchoXFlow. Seven modified upstream modules are subject to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The archive includes upstream licence, source mapping, provenance notice and file hashes. Other files have mixed or unverified provenance; no blanket licence is asserted. Scripts contain path placeholders and are not a standalone reproduction. Restricted files can be requested from the record owner, subject to applicable licences.

summary: Abstract The three companions [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] use three structures side by side: probability laws and kernels, provenance (which source a record came from), and differentiation at the boundary of the simplex. This paper studies how they fit together, one layer at a time. Every ingredient of Step 1 is standard in categorical probability; what this step contributes is a set of exact statements about where the ingredients fail to commute, which the later steps build on. The finite distribution monad Dand the provenance comonad W= L×(−) are related by a distributive law λ: WD⇒DW, (l,p) →δ l ⊗p. All four axioms are written out with their types and proved. Its two-sided Kleisli category is the category of Markov kernels indexed by a source, with one source held throughout a composite. Marginalisation is total and affine. Event conditioning is partial and nonlinear. It is undefined exactly where the event has probability zero, it cannot be extended continuously to that wall, and its derivative grows like 1/p(A) near it. Conditioning commutes with marginalisation only for events that are cylinders over the kept coordinates. Contextual Bayes decomposition. Conditioning a pooled law equals pooling the conditioned sources with Bayes-updated weights. In the worked example, source weights 1 3 4 , 4 become 8 15 23 , 23 , and keeping the old weights gives the wrong answer ( 63 160 instead of 9 23 ). Forgetting provenance is marginalisation over the sources. It commutes with every window, but it is not injective: two families of sources can share a pooled law and every pooled table while differing in every labelled table. Step 2, the tangent layer. The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. Each source is a face of the labelled simplex, and a feasible direction leaves that face exactly when it injects whole records under another label; after forgetting provenance, an injected source and a drifting source have the same direction. Marginalisation and conditioning map feasible cones onto feasible cones, with explicit lifts; conditioning’s lift shrinks like p(A) near its wall. The cone T k Hof the half-line is generated by elementary tensors, so it is closed under products, and pooling is a morphism at every order: the pooling paradox lives in the decision functional, not in pooling. Differentiating the contextual Bayes decomposition splits every sensitivity into a reweighting term and a within-source term; in the worked example the answer 9 16 23 moves at rate− 529 per unit of small-trial share. Strata and jumps. The sources that survive conditioning are exactly those with π l p l (A) > 0. Conditioning maps fibres of forgetting onto fibres: it keeps provenance ambiguity on the event, discards it off the event, and can destroy identifiability but never create it. Inside 1 its domain, conditioning moves at rate at most 2/P(A), so nothing jumps and a sudden change needs a rare event. At the wall the limit is the conditional of the path’s leading jet; analytic passages are removable, and jumps need a kink, a non-analytic path, or a jump of the law. Step 3, orders of transitions. On non-negative germs in a Hardy field, order is a semiring homomorphism to (min,+), so every layer operation has an exact order calculus. Each source reaches an event at its own order. The sources of least order survive conditioning, with weights given by leading coefficients; the others vanish at their extinction orders. The two sides of a transition carry independent order data, analytic passages are removable but smooth ones need not be, and flat approaches have limits inside a Hardy field but not outside. A transition of order mis invisible to the tangent tower below level m. At a fixed gap, a higher-order approach switches more gradually. Step 4a–4b, several parameters. When several rates vanish together, orders form a fan: the normal fan of a Newton pol

summary: Genetic mutations can lead to disease by disrupting molecular interactions, altering protein stability, inducing misfolding, and promoting protein aggregation. Although existing predictive models have achieved promising performance, they often lack mechanistic interpretability and fail to fully incorporate the underlying physical and chemical principles governing mutation-induced effects. Moreover, current approaches typically address disease association, protein stability changes, and solubility alterations as separate prediction tasks rather than integrating them within a unified framework. In this study, we introduce a multiscale commutative algebra modeling framework for predicting disease-mutation association. Leveraging persistent Stanley-Reisner theory, we extract algebraic invariants to build two predictive models: Commutative Algebra Neural Network (CANet) and Commutative Algebra Gradient Boosting Tree (CATree). The proposed framework is applied to three biologically connected tasks: disease-associated mutation identification, mutation-induced protein stability change prediction, and mutation-induced protein solubility change classification. Across six benchmark tasks, CANet and CATree consistently achieve leading predictive performance, with up to 7.5% relative improvement over existing methods. These results demonstrate that commutative algebra provides a unified, interpretable, and generalizable modeling strategy for mutation-disease association prediction.
title: Commutative Algebra Modeling of Mutation and Disease Association

The proposed framework is applied to three biologically connected tasks: disease-associated mutation identification, mutation-induced protein stability change prediction, and mutation-induced protein solubility change classification. Across six benchmark tasks, CANet and CATree consistently achieve leading predictive performance, with up to 7.5% relative improvement over existing methods. These results demonstrate that commutative algebra provides a unified, interpretable, and generalizable modeling strategy for mutation-disease association prediction.
title: Commutative Algebra Modeling of Mutation and Disease Association

summary: Abstract and Prior-Art Disclosure This manuscript serves as a formal public prior-art disclosure, conceptual research archive, and consolidated technical design dossier for the proposed Metric Spacetime Manipulator 26 (MSM-26) architecture. As the twenty-sixth revision and direct successor to MSM-25 Rev. 3, MSM-26 preserves the established architectural topology, chronological provenance, authorship, foundational subsystem configurations, and speculative physical mechanisms of the continuing Metric Spacetime Manipulator research program, while introducing substantial refinements to its flux-bias architecture, resonator construction, electromagnetic coupling configurations, operating principles, and associated engineering specifications. This revision supersedes MSM-25 Rev. 3 and all preceding MSM revisions, except where earlier configurations are explicitly retained as architectural inheritance or documented in the revision-comparison, errata, and reconciliation registers. MSM-26 specifies a cryogenic superconducting architecture whose active core consists of a closed, series-connected chain of Superconducting Nonlinear Asymmetric Inductive eLement (SNAIL) fluxonium cells , collectively designated the SNAILonium. Adjacent galvanically connected SNAIL elements possess alternating loop chirality, with each element incorporating exactly (n=3) large Josephson junctions and an associated small Josephson junction. The architecture retains its admissible superconducting conductor configurations, comprising the superconducting flat-wire ribbon and the contour-conformal coplanar-waveguide configuration, with the latter incorporating ground-plane boundaries that follow the SNAIL contour and locally widened gaps around the junction regions. The Josephson-junction interlayer retains three admissible configurations: a conventional dielectric insulating barrier, magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, and moiré-twisted (MoTe_2). The architecture retains three principal SNAILonium lumped-element resonance circuit configurations: the ring-shaped resonator, the flat bifilar Fermat spiral terminating in two tangentially and galvanically coupled SNAILonium rings, and the bifilar poloidal–toroidal helix arranged along closed toroidal geodesics. The third configuration further incorporates a dedicated second filar functioning concurrently as a flux-bias line and kinetic inductance resonator. The capacitive discontinuities may be implemented using vacuum air-bridge or interdigital capacitors. All three constructions are broadside coupled to the superconducting SNAILonium conductor carrying the (n=3) large junctions. summary: What's new in 1.13.1 ProvSQL 1.13.1 is a bug-fix release for bounded and interruptible evaluation . A provenance circuit loaded for evaluation could exceed provsql.max_memory before the limit was checked, a signal arriving during an exchange with the circuit-store worker could leave a backend waiting forever, and a cancel or statement_timeout did not reach a backend waiting on that worker. All three are fixed, circuits load faster and in less memory, and a new function, sr_formula_rows , gives the formula of a token whose sr_formula is too large to be produced as a single string. It also fixes two outer-join and HAVING shapes that were rejected. Memory limit and cancellation provsql.max_memory is enforced while the circuit is read. The store worker checked the budget once per gate, so a single gate with a very large number of wires (an aggregate over millions of rows, for instance) could be read in full before the check. It now checks per wire, and hashes gate names incrementally instead of building the whole name of a large gate first. The query fails with SQLSTATE 54000 instead of the backend being killed by the operating system. A signal no longer breaks an exchange with the store worker. A read or write on the pipe between a backend and the worker that was interrupted by a signal was not retried: a circuit could be sent only in part, leaving the backend waiting for an answer that would never come, or a message could be left half-read. Both directions now retry until the message is complete. Cancel and statement_timeout stop a backend waiting on the store. A backend waiting for the worker's answer, or for the lock that serializes access to it, now notices a cancel request or a statement timeout and raises the usual error. Faster circuit loading Circuits are loaded with a heap-based work list, one store lookup per gate and one hash per wire, and gate UUIDs are kept as 16 bytes instead of strings, which lowers both the time and the memory of every evaluation over a large circuit. sr_formula_rows sr_formula_rows(token, mapping, max_size) returns the formula of sr_formula as a set of (name, formula) rows of bounded size. Row #1 is the formula of the token; a sub-formula of more than max_size symbols (50 by default) is named #2 , #3 … and given a row of its own, and a sum or product with many terms is written with an ellipsis and its number of terms, its terms becoming rows #k.1 , #k.2 … Rows are produced one at a time, each reading only the part of the circuit it needs, so LIMIT , a cursor, or paging bound the work. Like sr_formula , it accepts any token type, so the aggregate of a subquery can be passed directly. Query rewriting Outer joins over an input that holds an outer join. When the input of an outer join contains an outer join itself, and an aggregate over it, the arms of the lowering read it from a shared CTE; a comparison on that aggregate is now recognized there, and an unmatched row yields one null-padded row, not one per value the aggregate takes. A join beside an outer join that reads a WITH entry of the statement is now rewritten correctly when it is moved into a subquery. HAVING added to any condition. When the rewriting adds a condition to an existing HAVING , it now wraps any Boolean condition (a function call, a CASE …), not only comparisons and Boolean operators. The set-operation column loop is bounded by an AttrNumber , and the safe-query column table is sized in Size . Platforms Compiler and linker warnings of the macOS and PostgreSQL 18 builds are fixed. PostgreSQL 18 is now tested on arm64 Linux in CI, and the documentation lists the tested platforms (native Windows is not supported; WSL is). Upgrading ALTER EXTENSION provsql UPDATE from 1.13.0 only creates sr_formula_rows . No gate type, type, operator, cast, or aggregate changes, and the circuit store format is unchanged.
title: ProvSQL: Semiring Provenance and Probability Management for PostgreSQL

summary: Paper P10 of a ten part series P1-P10 on Interaction, Cohesive Emergence, and Fundamental Constants in Generalised Trace Dynamics P10 — Synthesis, physical compatibility and fundamental constants Can the exceptional algebras that organise candidate particle properties also describe the dynamics that selects them? We give a pedagogical research synthesis of nine studies of interacting generalised trace dynamics and its finite matrix extensions. Interactions between spacetime--matter atoms are motivated by bosonic exchange between fermionic currents. An ordered coassociative vertex, its graded selection rules and a positive mediated kernel make this proposal calculable. A selected physical-current model has a common onset of two neutral composite condensates, while separate matrix parents exhibit exact ordering bounds, competing geometric configurations and finite-time record protocols. A trace isometry connects a spin-one matrix sector to exceptional Jordan invariants. For one exact canonical fermion determinant, a positive-squares identity proves that commuting equilateral configurations, rather than the Jordan-bearing balanced branch, are selected sufficiently close to onset. A complementary exact result shows that the polynomial parent's cubic selects associative orientations of the balanced spin-one branch, whose centred Jordan spectrum is a degenerate doublet. Equal spacing is not stationary under those unrestricted orientation variations. Massive canonical fermions can provide positive local orientation curvature, but cancellation of the cubic slope and full vacuum stability are separate conditions. A further fixed-charge parent supports a stable local branch whose Jordan response requires additional collective coordinates. Conserved charges then produce a calculable, coordinate-invariant difference between relaxed static and closed-system slow spectral response. These results put earlier mass-ratio, mixing and gauge-normalisation proposals into contact with explicit vacuum and response calculations. They also identify their remaining inputs: the microscopic physical projection, state, relative family frames, kinetic residues and matching data. Full cohesive emergence of spacetime, matter and classical records, and the measured fundamental constants, have not been derived. The interaction is required to preserve the additive STM sector's conditional spectral framework. Recovery at zero coupling does not establish this compatibility at finite coupling; we formulate the missing projection and backreaction tests explicitly. The achievement is a set of constructive bridges and discriminating tests, with a concrete route from algebraic hypotheses to physical predictions.

summary: R code, data and computed output accompanying the manuscript “The Unit-Truncated Power Bilal Distribution: Structural Properties, Shape Analysis, and Statistical Inference” by Preut Thanarat, Tharakorn Jaruruataikant and Nipada Papukdee. The deposit is organised in two parts. round1/ holds the five R scripts of the original submission and their output: the theoretical PDF, CDF and hazard-rate figures; the structural summaries, quantile-based shape measures and entropies; the Monte Carlo study over eight parameter configurations and five sample sizes, including observed-information standard errors and empirical Wald coverage; and the FirmCost and SC16 applications with parametric-bootstrap goodness-of-fit calibration, the likelihood-ratio test of the nested unit-truncated Bilal restriction, and the CDF, TTT and Q-Q diagnostics. round2/ holds the revision package as it was run. It adds the expanded comparison of nine named model specifications across four source datasets (FirmCost, SC16, AIS and College) and eight analysis groups, with parametric-bootstrap Cramér–von Mises and Anderson–Darling diagnostics at B = 999 and repeated five-fold cross-validation; the College interval-observation likelihood under an assumed nearest-percentage-point rounding mechanism; the limiting-likelihood and boundary-information analysis; the four source datasets together with the archived cross-validation fold assignments, so the predictive comparisons reproduce exactly; and the computed tables and vector figures. A SHA256 manifest is included for verification, and reference/ preserves the original Monte Carlo and goodness-of-fit sources, including the analytic audit of 6,000 replications. All results were produced in R 4.6.1 using the parallel package with a PSOCK cluster and ggplot2 for the figures; the round-two stages also require the sn package. Random seeds, optimizer settings and the boundary-fit classification rule are documented in README.md. Released under the MIT License.
title: Replication code and output for "The Unit-Truncated Power Bilal Distribution: Structural Properties, Shape Analysis, and Statistical Inference

summary: When a security commitment is defended by an organised interest, the interest may have preceded the commitment, grown out of it, or been built on purpose by its sponsor. These three readings come from interest-group research, policy-feedback research and research on designing policies to last, and are rarely set side by side. We make them testable and apply them to attempts to end security commitments in the United States and Europe after 1945. The dependent variable is the survival of a commitment under an attempt to reverse it, not the level of spending. In the United States cases (the B-1 bomber, the F-22 and C-17, the F136 alternate engine, the closure of military bases, and all programmes proposed for termination in 2009), the breadth of a programme's supplier spread does not decide its survival: the F-22 and the C-17, with suppliers in 44 and 43 states, had opposite fates in 2009. Three findings follow. The legislature's own record can be the defending interest: programmes Congress had created or restored against the executive survived where programmes it had merely funded did not. Executive pressure can be graded from the Statements of Administration Policy: the only unconditional veto threat ended its programme, while conditional threats and objections did not end programmes Congress owned. And what protects a commitment is whether its central defenders can be compensated, down to the production site. In Europe, as the European Defence Fund's rules are rewritten, the veto member states wrote for themselves is extended while the Commission's rule for spreading benefits is made optional. We register one prediction on the Fund's successor. The evidence extends to material published on 1 November 2026, including reporting on member-state divisions over the European Competitiveness Fund.
title: Grown or Built? Interests that Defend Commitments after 1945

The cone tangent structure of the tangent companion commutes with the provenance comonad. summary: This Python software provides a Docker-based workflow for electroencephalography (EEG) quality control, preprocessing and feature extraction . It supports reproducible research on attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) in children and adolescents using the task recordings in the BALLADEER dataset. The software documents and implements the processing workflow underlying A task EEG dataset with preprocessed signals and features for ADHD research in children and adolescents . That companion resource contains 669 eligible recordings from 156 participants and 115 feature definitions or templates across seven feature families. The recordings and generated feature tables are distributed separately from this software. What the software does Raw EEG quality assessment: characterizes recording quality before preprocessing and produces structured quality summaries. Recording eligibility and correction plans: applies the supplied, frozen label-blind selection records, including recording eligibility and approved channel-interpolation actions. Conservative EEG preprocessing: processes continuous blocks without bridging acquisition gaps, applies 0.5–40 Hz filtering, harmonizes sampling to 128 Hz, and performs conditional channel interpolation and average referencing. Post-preprocessing quality assessment: calculates quality summaries and comparisons with the original recordings. EEG feature extraction: generates seven feature families using aligned, gap-aware windows of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds with 50% overlap, subject to each estimator's duration requirements. Output verification: checks processing lineage, cross-stage consistency and recorded checksums. The supplied selection records preserve the decisions used for the companion dataset. Reusing those records does not repeat the original manual review or establish new eligibility decisions for another cohort. Seven EEG feature families Temporal and statistical features. Conventional spectral features. Aperiodic spectral features. Complexity and fractal features. Functional connectivity features. Graph and network features. Time-frequency decomposition features. Feature definitions expand across channels, channel pairs and other indexed positions. Outputs retain calculation states and reasons for unavailable or undefined values. Duration-dependent support is explicit; for example, the configured aperiodic spectral analysis uses 8- and 16-second windows. Supported recordings, inputs and outputs The input is the original BALLADEER dataset, version 2 , obtained from its version-specific Figshare record . Extract the source data before running the software. Set --input-dir to the directory that directly contains users_demographics.json and participant directories such as UB0004/ , preserving the original task subdirectories and filenames. The companion Zenodo derivative dataset is an output resource, not the input to this complete reproduction workflow. The packaged workflow is configured for five BALLADEER task conditions: CogniFit cognitive assessment, Attention Robots, and Slackline levels 1, 6 and 11. Users also provide a writable output directory. The input directory is mounted read-only. Outputs include preprocessed EEG signals in MNE-FIF format, tabular feature outputs, quality summaries, calculation-state records, configuration snapshots, processing manifests and checksums. The software archive includes label-blind selection metadata with pseudonymous recording identifiers; it does not contain the original EEG recordings or the generated derivative dataset. Reproducibility and package contents The archive includes Python source code, scientific configurations, a Dockerfile, version-pinned Python dependencies, shell launchers, validation tests and documentation. Users can run individual processing stages, extract one feature family for one task, or execute the complete sequential workflow. Graph features use the corresponding connectivity outputs. summary: APEP — JGR manuscript release ( paper-jgr-v1.0 ) Code, data products and figures supporting the manuscript on the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs). Summary We present a multipoint investigation of the ionospheric response to the 14 October 2023 annular and 8 April 2024 total Great American Eclipses (GAEs) using coordinated observations from five Digisondes, the Wallops Island VIPIR, the Millstone Hill incoherent scatter radar, and continental-scale GNSS TEC measurements. Key results Clear E- and F2-region depletions in both events across peak obscurations of 0.30–0.82, observed at local times 10:24–15:22 LT. E region depletion scales quasi-linearly with obscuration; the F2 region lags peak obscuration by 20–30 min, consistent with the longer O⁺ recombination timescale. No G-condition (NmF1 ≥ NmF2) in either event, even at 0.82 obscuration: high obscuration alone is insufficient without adequate F2-peak height reduction and favourable local-time/seasonal conditions. White Sands skymaps show a bifurcated echo population during the 2024 recovery phase; Wallops VIPIR frequency–time–intensity plots show cusp-like features confined to 3–6 MHz. Idealized ray tracing shows both signatures can arise from eclipse-excited wave structures at different horizontal scales, i.e. distinct HF manifestations of a common wave field. GNSS TEC : along-track relative change in minima exceeds 40 % (2023 and 2024) relative to the expected baseline. Figures in this release All manuscript figures are in manuscript_figures/jgr/ (PNG, plus PDF where produced). Generating code is in apep/jgr/ . Figures 2 and 4 (ionosonde time series) were redone as 5×4 grids: rows are the five stations sorted by peak obscuration; columns are foF2, h′F2/hmF2, foE, h′E/hmE. Each panel shows the eclipse-day series (smoothed, gaps ≤ 90 min interpolated) against the quiet-day median, with the eclipse interval shaded and the peak obscuration 𝒪ᵖ₁₉₃ annotated. Journal-style fonts, thin lines, no heavy markers; AGU double-column width. Figure 2 (2023, 13–21 UT) is built entirely from Datasets/Data/*_scaled.csv and *_median.csv ; WS833/KR835 use the despiked event files in Datasets/processing/final/ when present. Figure 4 (2024, 16–21 UT) is built from SAO data via jgr_2024_scaled.py . Shared code: apep/jgr/jgr_timeseries_5x4.py ( jgr_2023_scaled.py is a thin wrapper). Known data caveats AU930 h′E sits in 100–110 km steps against an ~85 km median (2023); the 2024 AU930 hmE median CSV is flat at 110 km. AU930 foF2 saturates near 9.9 MHz after ~18:30 UT (2023). BC840 h′F2 shows a ~340 km excursion near maximum obscuration (2023). KR835/WS833 median CSVs lack true hmF2/hmE; 2024 KR835/WS833 median CSVs do not exist (baseline falls back to the SAO mean); WS833 2024 has no data. Reproducing the time-series figures conda run -n apep python -m apep.jgr.jgr_timeseries_5x4 --year 2023 # Figure 2 conda run -n apep python apep/jgr/jgr_2024_scaled.py # Figure 4

summary: 50/60 MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT MISSION RELIABILITY IN AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC REGENERATIVE MANUFACTURING AT THE LIMIT is a 777-page English-language Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Micro/Nanorobot Fabrication and Regenerative Biomanufacturing Sixty-Flagship series (Flagship 50/60). It investigates safe failure recovery with preserved productive service. The research coupling is autonomous manufacturing mission x regenerative specimen integrity x physically verified fault recovery. All proposed work is restricted to nonclinical in-vitro, organ-on-chip, synthetic phantom or authorized ex-vivo environments. No experiments were executed in preparing this edition; no human treatment, clinical efficacy or regulatory clearance is claimed. Its falsifiable candidate is: A frozen safety and recovery protocol will improve completed qualified work at equal fault burden while meeting independent stop and specimen integrity gates. The Atlas minimum demonstrator is: Blind-inject four fault classes into complete cell assembly missions with matched useful work targets. Strong comparators include expert human operation, fixed automation scripts and conventional redundant hardware. A central rival account is apparent safety caused by aborting early and completing less useful work. The nonnegotiable stop condition is: no advantage at equal effective work or an unknown fault fails to stop the apparatus. Each failed, aborted, hidden-fault and incomplete run is retained in the experimental denominator, and observation of a finished form is never substituted for independently measured function. Thirty mathematical plates address domain-specific metrics and established model families across transport, measurement, elasticity, time-dependent dynamics, causal attribution, calibration and uncertainty. Eighty-two chapters and 410 separately paginated scientific investigations organize six research arcs. Two hundred Research Gates have been revised with independent observables, one of fifteen blinded causal intervention families, orthogonal controls and noncompensatory refusal criteria. Thirty mathematical plates now carry model-specific physical derivation commentary, explicit applicability limits and distinct flagship-level blind checks. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose unbuilt future instruments and succession artifacts, each requiring its own bench validation. This version is a research design and not a report of validated physical findings. It draws scientific method and conceptual boundaries from the user-supplied Atlas and research mother volumes; especially the Atlas-supplied ancestry DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020. Full external bibliographic DOI checking and scientific peer review have not been completed. Domain-specific sensitivity, causal identifiability and independent replication require qualified laboratory evaluation before any scientific superiority claim. summary: Abstract: Classical inferential statistics and p-value hypothesis testing in healthcare big data repositories suffer from severe structural limitations, notably p-hacking, asymptotic N-bias, and the frequent violation of independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) assumptions due to intra-patient longitudinal dependencies, hospital clustering, and epidemiological shockwaves. To overcome these failures, we introduce an Inverse Breakpoint Analysis, a scale-invariant, physics-inspired metrological audit framework. Our analysis treats discrete clinical event counts not as abstract probabilities, but as physical informational mass. Grounded in Garwood exact discrete limits and Wilson-Hilferty approximations, the framework extends our previous work on stress testing indices for Big health data and establishes three rigorous thresholds: a pure mass saturation limit, a baseline tolerance band, and a structural signal threshold. Through the use of these three parameters, our inverse break-point analysis eliminates false-positive artifacts induced by massive repository sizes while preventing under-powering in small cohorts. Ultimately, the framework demonstrates that percentage-based thresholds are kinematic artifacts of scale, whereas absolute excess discrete mass serves as the sole physical invariant for healthcare data validation. We validated this approach with numerous illustrative examples.
title: Inverse Breakpoint Analysis: A Scale-Invariant Physics-Inspired Metrological Audit for Sanitary Big Data

summary: Flagship 60/60 Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? TRUSTWORTHY AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC MANUFACTURING PLATFORMS FOR REGENERATIVE MEDICINE AT THE LIMIT This 777-page Research Design Working Edition in the STARLI Nano Regenerative Biomanufacturing series investigates bounded autonomous manufacturing under explicit authorization and independent release. Its scientific coupling is nanorobotics x autonomous biomanufacturing x regenerative quality governance. The evidence perimeter is prospective and nonclinical, using closed in-vitro systems, organ-on-chip platforms or authorized ex-vivo material; neither clinical efficacy nor autonomous human intervention is claimed. The falsifiable question is: Can distributed research stations preserve qualified biosafe work and genuine operator exit when suppliers, control versions or core services disappear? The proposed minimum demonstration is: Two independent community laboratories reconstruct and release nonclinical mock devices from a shared open evidence package. Strong comparators include centralized controlled manufacture, skilled manual labs and single-vendor automation. The central competing explanation is distributed autonomy secretly dependent on centralized reagents, controls or calibration. The noncompensatory stop rule is: operator exit becomes impossible, site performance gap grows or minimum safe service is interrupted. Every eligible, stopped, refused and unsuccessful experiment belongs to the full denominator. Thirty conditional mathematical plates specify different analytic roles, measurements, units and blind failure tests. Eighty-two chapters contain 410 individual research investigations. Two hundred Research Gates organize twenty causal challenge families across ten primary physical observables, each with an independently read companion, concealed intervention, matched comparator, explicit rival and refusal gate. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose future experimental and evidence instruments. All are experimental plans rather than executed observations. The source Atlas and methodology ancestors provide reference architecture but do not establish the new integrated candidate. Source-supplied ancestry includes 10.5281/zenodo.23046134 and 10.5281/zenodo.23486020; source-associated external DOI candidates must be bibliographically checked before citation. summary: Tomographic reconstruction is challenging because of limited angular coverage, noise, specimen motion and radiation damage. Here, I present GRECO, Geometric Registration of Electron Cryotomography Observations, an algorithm that uses local specimen structure to fit a shared three-dimensional geometry. Starting from central views, it selects landmarks from a working reconstruction and progressively adds neighbouring views. Near zero tilt, uncertainty in landmark depth has less effect on the predicted image position, allowing provisional landmarks to guide the first steps. Each landmark contributes through views with useful local information. For each observation, GRECO reconstructs a local reference from the other supporting views and compensates for the directional blur produced by those viewing angles. A joint fit updates image translations and landmark positions, linking overlapping angular tracks across the series. GRECO produced reconstructions suitable for subtomogram averaging, detection of small macromolecular complexes and detailed membrane segmentation across specimens ranging from vesicles with fiducials and a fiducial-free mixture to an intact near-minimal cell and cellular lamellae imaged in situ. The Greco software combines this registration algorithm with fast preprocessing, reconstruction and TinyCARE denoising, providing a practical workflow for studying molecular structure and cellular organization.
title: GRECO: Geometric Registration of Electron Cryotomography Observations

summary: Genetic mutations can lead to disease by disrupting molecular interactions, altering protein stability, inducing misfolding, and promoting protein aggregation. Although existing predictive models have achieved promising performance, they often lack mechanistic interpretability and fail to fully incorporate the underlying physical and chemical principles governing mutation-induced effects. Moreover, current approaches typically address disease association, protein stability changes, and solubility alterations as separate prediction tasks rather than integrating them within a unified framework. In this study, we introduce a multiscale commutative algebra modeling framework for predicting disease-mutation association. Leveraging persistent Stanley-Reisner theory, we extract algebraic invariants to build two predictive models: Commutative Algebra Neural Network (CANet) and Commutative Algebra Gradient Boosting Tree (CATree). The proposed framework is applied to three biologically connected tasks: disease-associated mutation identification, mutation-induced protein stability change prediction, and mutation-induced protein solubility change classification. Across six benchmark tasks, CANet and CATree consistently achieve leading predictive performance, with up to 7.5% relative improvement over existing methods. These results demonstrate that commutative algebra provides a unified, interpretable, and generalizable modeling strategy for mutation-disease association prediction.
title: Commutative Algebra Modeling of Mutation and Disease Association

summary: Generative models are increasingly used for circuit synthesis and optimization by proposing topologies, sizing devices, and exploring large design spaces. We investigate whether they can instead support design discovery, where generated structures must depart from known designs while producing reproducible electrical behavior. We propose Delta-Seeker, a closed-loop circuit search framework that combines discrete diffusion for topology generation and mutation with structural checking, SPICE-in-the-loop sizing, Pareto selection, and feedback from prior search outcomes. The search controller uses progress and recurring structural failures to allocate evaluation effort and steer subsequent topology generation, while independent re-sizing and operating-corner analysis are performed only after search. In generator-only experiments, cross-generation feedback increases structurally valid children from 143 to 945 and reduces the faulty-candidate fraction from 0.925 to 0.761. In op-amp topology discovery at matched sizing cost, Delta-Seeker yields 54 designs that remain feasible in at least three of four independent re-sizings and 18 that additionally pass device-level checks and supply-temperature corner analysis, compared with 38 and 10 under fixed control. Removing cross-generation memory reduces independently robust discoveries from 54 to 43 and seven-corner robust discoveries from 40 to 27. In DC-DC converter search, nearest-parent analysis identifies a corpus-absent topology whose generated switching current path changes its nearest training-corpus parent from infeasible at all four operating corners to feasible at all four, while increasing median efficiency from 31.2% to 98.96%. These results show that closed-loop generative search can support circuit discovery beyond structural novelty by identifying new topologies with independently verified changes in circuit operation.
title: Delta-Seeker: Closed-Loop Generative Search for Novel Circuit Design Discovery

summary: Real-world image editing requires coordinating multiple visual transformations with content preservation and reference constraints, yet aggregate scores can readily obscure unmet local requirements. Effective evaluation must therefore identify local failures and translate them into priorities for subsequent model improvement. We introduce WeGenEditBench, comprising 2,740 evaluation instances and 148 task types across single-image, text-intensive, and multi-reference editing. Pre-generated checklists shared across models decompose each request into atomic requirements; item-level deductions and visual evidence are established first and then summarized into scores for edit execution, preservation, visual quality, and task-specific correctness. To support the experience-acquisition component of recursive self-improvement (RSI), we develop WeGenEvoStudio, a unified multi-agent harness for RSI-oriented learning that integrates model-conditioned failure diagnosis, retrieval-grounded data construction, supervised adaptation, and re-evaluation. Among 15 evaluated configurations, GPT-Image-2 leads single-image editing with an Overall score of 4.076, while Seedream-5.0-Pro leads text-intensive editing at 4.291. Evolution experiments across four generation and editing benchmarks demonstrate substantial targeted gains: on their report-selected Top-5 single-image targets, FLUX.2 [dev] improves Overall from 1.083 to 3.517, while Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 gains 13.2%. Together, our benchmark and harness provide a foundation for developing more reliable image models through interpretable evaluation and feedback-driven learning.
title: From Evaluation to Evolution: Benchmarking Image Editing and Evolving Image Models

summary: In text-to-SQL and AI-agent analytics, successful SQL execution does not establish semantic correctness under changing business definitions. We study revalidation of fixed queries after changes to refund attribution, tax treatment, eligible populations and exchange-rate dates. An executable verification profile binds the requested revision and knowledge cutoff to legal counterexample data and exact monetary comparison. A preregistered confirmation on 32 newly authored revision families and two local producer bundles retains 192 query-definition cells: 144 nonconforming, 36 finite-suite agreeing and 12 unresolved. Of the nonconforming cells, 63 agree on the current snapshot. At an eight-ledger budget, obligation-guided checking detects 137 discrepancies versus 127 for generic ordering, a paired difference of 6.9 percentage points (family bootstrap 95% interval [2.1, 13.6]; exact family sign-flip p=0.0156). Every ledger arm rejects zero of the 36 agreeing cells. Current-obligation and equal-weight scoring match the guided result, identifying coverage rather than revision-specific priority as the observed source of benefit. Controlled assays, a natural-query pilot and repeated samples provide separate mechanism and robustness evidence. A legal discrepancy refutes conformance; agreement remains restricted to the recorded suite. The study establishes an auditable business-semantic revalidation profile within its authored schema and local-model scope.

summary: Steering vectors (SVs) are residual-stream directions that shift the behavior of LLMs when added to hidden states at inference time. While prior work has mainly used SVs as post-hoc controls, we ask whether the same directions can also guide parameter updates during post-training. We study this question across supervised learning, including SFT and distillation, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Our framework considers two intervention regimes: a hidden-state hook during teacher-forced supervised training, and an advantage-repair mechanism on wrong rollouts in GRPO. For each regime, we analyze three design axes, which are the steering direction, its placement, and the operation used to combine it with training. In supervised settings, SV injection improves over plain SFT and distillation, with gains scaling with the off-policy gap and reaching up to a $12\%$ improvement when distilling from thinking-mode teachers. These gains hold across three random seeds. In RL settings, applying a correctness-contrast direction as advantage repair on wrong rollouts, including otherwise zero-gradient all-wrong groups, recovers a learning signal that transfers to held-out math benchmarks and acts as a composable auxiliary signal that adds to existing zero-variance remedies such as entropy-aware advantage shaping. We further identify three failure boundaries. In detail, code generation can break the direction, cross-family layer transfer can break the placement, and inference-time application on an SV-trained checkpoint can break the intervention regime. Together, these results establish steering vectors as a conditional but effective training signal for LLM post-training. Our code is available here.
title: Steering Vectors as a Training Signal in LLM Post-Training

summary: Human preferences change over time: an established preference may remain valid over time, become uncertain as context shifts, or be explicitly revised. Effective personalization requires conversational AI to adapt its response strategy to evolving preferences rather than relying on passive memory retrieval. We formalize this capability as adaptive personalization under epistemic uncertainty. A human preference study further confirms that people favor state-contingent response strategies as preference uncertainty changes. To evaluate whether language models mirror this adaptation, we create a multilingual benchmark spanning 250 personas, 5 languages, and 25K conversational turns that decouples strategy selection from response execution. Across eight closed- and open-weight models, we uncover a recognition-generation gap: models reliably identify appropriate strategies when selecting among candidate options, but collapse during open-ended generation, suffering a 35-46% drop in strategy calibration. Crucially, this failure is systematic: models default to exploit-first behavior, over-relying on existing preferences regardless of preference epistemic uncertainty. We show this failure is addressable: while prompting interventions fail, targeted training that supervises models' internal strategy representations toward state-conditional human preferences narrows the user acceptability generalization gap by a third on out-of-distribution personas and conversational styles.

summary: The semidefinite programs (SDPs) of the numerical conformal bootstrap, and of S-matrix and quantum-mechanics bootstraps, are solved with primal-dual interior-point methods whose convergence guarantees rest on primal and dual Slater conditions: the existence of strictly feasible points on both sides of the duality. Many bootstrap SDPs violate these. The consequences range from slow convergence to inconclusive verdicts and the breakdown of the Skydive algorithm. We introduce "Slater tools", all acting within the PMP class accepted by SDPB. Diagnostics measure the Slater margins and, when a margin vanishes, extract the exposing certificate that identifies the degeneracy. Two independent cures follow. Transforms that provide rigorous bounds on the original SDP objective and that for the right parameter choices return the exact value. Facial reductions that use the exposing certificate to remove the degeneracies themselves. We reproduce, explain and resolve all known types of failures in a mixed-correlator 3d Ising setup. We show that the $X$-Slater condition (SDPB's primal) fails at every disallowed point in feasibility mode, holds in every navigator problem we tested, and can be guaranteed by one additional condition on the navigator function. We show that the folklore "instability remedy" of a twist gap works by removing degeneracies at the endpoints of the positivity conditions. These often stem from a mistake in factoring out the block prefactor but can also arise legitimately in channels that mix equal and unequal operator pairs. Finally we classify and remove all degeneracies of the published current-scalar bootstrap, among them one at $x=\infty$, thus incurable by any gap assumption, caused by unequal polynomial degrees within one matrix block.

summary: LUNA is a differentiable astrophysical hydrodynamics code written in JAX, with hand-written Pallas kernels as a fast path on GPUs. It solves the Euler equations in one, two and three dimensions with an unsplit, second-order MUSCL-Hancock scheme and HLLC or HLL Riemann solvers, and runs on CPUs and on many NVIDIA or AMD GPUs, with the domain split over devices. Self-gravity is solved with periodic or isolated boundaries and couples to the gas conserving energy; comoving cosmology evolves gas together with dark-matter particles; radiative cooling, driven turbulence and starburst energy and mass injection are built in. Examples of what it does: shock tubes, blast waves and Kelvin-Helmholtz, Rayleigh-Taylor and Richtmyer-Meshkov instabilities; Jeans collapse and collapsing self-gravitating clouds; the cosmic web of gas and dark matter from cosmological initial conditions; driven supersonic turbulence; galactic winds blown out of a starburst disk; and inverse problems, such as optimising initial conditions with gradients taken through the solver. Non-equilibrium chemistry and cooling networks, radiation transport, sink particles and star formation with stellar dynamics and feedback through Torch/AMUSE, and block-based adaptive mesh refinement are included as experimental modules. Validated capabilities are tested against exact solutions or other codes (AthenaK, Arepo, RAMSES), whose reference solutions are published with the code.
